from_module(*as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Puts the parameters and buffers of a module in a tensordict.

The entries are the parameters and buffers of the module themselves,
not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Note

This method does not lock the result by default (`lock=False`).
The function [`tensordict.from_module()`](tensordict.from_module.html#tensordict.from_module) locks it by default
(`lock=True`).

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance is returned, which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `False`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Use it when the module has
state-dict hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no
entry. If `False`, they get an empty tensordict.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> list(params.keys())
['0']
>>> params.is_locked
False
```

*classmethod*from_tensordict(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *non_tensordict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Wraps a tensordict in a new instance of the tensorclass, without copying the leaves.

If `tensordict` is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), the entries of the fields
annotated with a tensorclass (or `Optional` of one) that are tensordicts become
instances of that tensorclass, recursively. They are set in a shallow copy of
`tensordict`, which keeps its own entries. An entry with keys that the annotated
class does not declare stays a tensordict. Other backends are wrapped as they are:
setting a tensorclass in them would write to their storage (e.g. an H5 file).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict that holds the tensor fields.
- **non_tensordict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the values of the non-tensor fields. The
fields that neither argument holds are set to `None`.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - Deprecated in 0.15, to be removed in TensorDict 0.17. Whether to
raise an error if `tensordict` is not a [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase).
Without it, such a tensordict raises an error.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Pose(TensorClass):
... q: torch.Tensor
>>> class Obs(TensorClass):
... a: Pose
>>> obs = Obs(a=Pose(q=torch.zeros(5, 4), batch_size=[5]), batch_size=[5])
>>> type(Obs.from_tensordict(obs.to_tensordict()).a).__name__
'Pose'
```

where(*condition: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *other: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *pad: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *update_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → T

Returns the elements of `self` where `condition` is `True`, and those of `other` elsewhere.

When `other` is a `NonTensorData` with another value, or a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack), the result is a [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) with
the value that `condition` picks for each element, or a
`NonTensorData` when all the elements have the same value. This
reads `condition`, which breaks the graph under [`torch.compile()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html#torch.compile).
Otherwise, the result has the value of `self` everywhere.

`out` receives the result if it can hold it. A `NonTensorData`
`out` cannot hold a [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack): the stack is returned,
and `out` is left as it is. [`TensorDict.where()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.where.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.where) then writes the
stack in place of the entry of its own `out`. See
[`TensorDictBase.where()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.where.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.where) for the arguments.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData
>>> a = NonTensorData("a", batch_size=[3])
>>> b = NonTensorData("b", batch_size=[3])
>>> a.where(torch.tensor([True, False, True]), b).tolist()
['a', 'b', 'a']
```

# NonTensorDataBase

`NonTensorDataBase` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `NonTensorDataBase` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.NonTensorDataBase(*data: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, *_metadata: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *_is_non_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***, *batch_size*, *device=None*, *names=None*)

Bases: [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass)

A base class for tensordict entries that hold a Python object instead of a tensor.

There are two subclasses:

- [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) holds one value per batch element.
Stacking or `unsqueeze` gives a [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack).
- [`MetaData`](tensordict.MetaData.html#tensordict.MetaData) holds one value for the whole batch.
Stacking items that hold the same object (checked with `is`) gives
one [`MetaData`](tensordict.MetaData.html#tensordict.MetaData) with the new batch size. Other items
give a [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack). `unsqueeze` and indexing
keep a [`MetaData`](tensordict.MetaData.html#tensordict.MetaData).

See [Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](../../concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data).

# NonTensorStack

`NonTensorStack` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `NonTensorStack` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.NonTensorStack(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict)

A lazy stack of [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData), one value per batch element.

You get a `NonTensorStack` when you stack
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) (or `NonTensorStack`) instances
with [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack), or when you assign a list to a key:
`td["names"] = ["a", "b", "c"]`. You can also build one with
`NonTensorStack("a", "b")` or `NonTensorStack.from_list(["a", "b"])`.

To read the values, call `tolist()`. `td["names"]` returns a
[`LinkedList`](tensordict.utils.LinkedList.html#tensordict.utils.LinkedList) of the values, and
`td.get("names")` returns the `NonTensorStack` itself. If every
element holds the same value, `data` returns it. To keep one shared
value for the whole batch, use [`MetaData`](tensordict.MetaData.html#tensordict.MetaData). See
[Non-tensor data and unbatched entries](../../concepts/non_tensor.html#non-tensor-data).

`torch.utils._pytree.tree_unflatten` and `tree_map` rebuild a
`NonTensorStack` entry of a tensordict whose values are all equal
from the input, as a [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData), and drop the value
that the function returned for it; they warn when that changes the result.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to keeping the
returned value, as they do when the values differ.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData, NonTensorStack, TensorDict
>>> NonTensorStack("a", "b").tolist()
['a', 'b']
>>> td = TensorDict(batch_size=[3])
>>> td["names"] = ["a", "b", "c"]
>>> td["names"]
LinkedList(['a', 'b', 'c'])
>>> td[1]["names"]
'b'
>>> type(td.get("names")).__name__
'NonTensorStack'
>>> data = torch.stack([
... torch.stack([NonTensorData(data=(i, j), batch_size=[]) for i in range(2)])
... for j in range(3)])
>>> print(data)
NonTensorStack(
 [[(0, 0), (1, 0)], [(0, 1), (1, 1)], [(0, 2), (1, ...,
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 2]),
 device=None)
```

*property*data*: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*

Returns the value of the stack, if every element holds the same value.

Raises:

[**AttributeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#AttributeError) - if the elements hold different values. Use
 `tolist()` to read them.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData
>>> torch.stack([NonTensorData("x"), NonTensorData("x")]).data
'x'
```

*classmethod*from_nontensordata(*non_tensor: [NonTensorData](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)*)

Expands a [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) into a stack of copies of it.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use `NonTensorData.maybe_to_stack()` instead. It differs in
two ways: its elements share the data object of `non_tensor`,
whereas this method copies it into every element; and when
`non_tensor` has an empty batch size, it returns `non_tensor`
itself, whereas this method returns a copy.

maybe_to_stack()

Placeholder for interchangeability between stack and non-stack of non-tensors.

tolist(***, *convert_nodes: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *convert_tensors: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['numpy'] = False*, *tolist_first: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *as_linked_list: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Extracts the content of a `tensordict.tensorclass.NonTensorStack` in a nested list.

Keyword Arguments:

- **convert_nodes** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - accepted for compatibility with
[`tolist()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.tolist). It has no effect:
the elements are the stored values, not tensordicts. Default: `True`.
- **convert_tensors** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if `True`, tensors will be converted to lists.
Otherwise, they will remain as tensors. Default: `False`.
- **tolist_first** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the tensordict will be converted to a list first when
it has batch dimensions. Default: `False`.
- **as_linked_list** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the list will be converted to a [`tensordict.utils.LinkedList`](tensordict.utils.LinkedList.html#tensordict.utils.LinkedList)
which will automatically update the tensordict when the list is modified. Default: `False`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import NonTensorData
>>> import torch
>>> data = torch.stack([
... torch.stack([NonTensorData(data=(i, j), batch_size=[]) for i in range(2)])
... for j in range(3)])
>>> data.tolist()
[[(0, 0), (1, 0)], [(0, 1), (1, 1)], [(0, 2), (1, 2)]]
```

# PackLayout

*class*tensordict.PackLayout(*keys: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), ...]*, *shapes: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size), ...]*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = -1*, *nested: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size), [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)], ...] = ()*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *cls: [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The layout of a tensordict packed by [`pack()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack).

It records the column of each leaf in the packed tensor, and the nesting,
batch dimensions and classes needed to rebuild the tensordict with
`unpack()`. It is frozen, hashable and compares by value, so a module
can cache it and `torch.compile` can treat it as a constant.

Only tensorclasses are rebuilt with their class. Other subclasses of
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase), such as
[`TypedTensorDict`](tensordict.TypedTensorDict.html#tensordict.TypedTensorDict) or
`TensorDictParams`, come back as a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Variables:

- **keys** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the leaf keys in column order.
- **shapes** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)) - the feature shape of each leaf, that is
its shape after the batch dimensions of the packed tensordict.
Lists and tuples of ints are converted to `torch.Size`.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the position of the packed dimension in the packed tensor.
[`pack()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.pack) stores it counted from the
end (a negative int), so `td.pack(1)` and `td.pack(-1)` give
equal layouts when `td` has one batch dimension, and `flat`
may have extra leading batch dimensions.
- **nested** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) - one `(key, batch_shape, cls)` entry per nested tensor
collection, where `batch_shape` is its batch shape after the
batch dimensions of the root and `cls` is its tensorclass, or
`None` for a tensordict. Batch shapes given as lists or tuples
of ints are converted to `torch.Size`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**None*) - the device of the packed tensordict.
- **cls** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*or**None*) - the tensorclass of the packed tensordict, or `None`.
- **offsets** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the first column of each leaf.
- **numel** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the number of columns of the packed tensor.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(p=torch.zeros(5), v=torch.ones(5, 3), batch_size=[5])
>>> flat, layout = td.pack()
>>> layout.keys, layout.offsets, layout.numel
(('p', 'v'), (0, 1), 4)
>>> out = layout.unpack(flat[:2])
>>> out["v"].shape
torch.Size([2, 3])
```

unpack(*flat: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Rebuilds a tensordict from a packed tensor.

The leaves of the result are views of `flat`. Its batch size is the
shape of `flat` without the packed dimension, so `flat` may have
other batch dimensions than the packed tensordict, for instance after
an `index_select`.

Parameters:

**flat** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - a tensor with `numel` entries along
dimension `dim`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or an instance of `cls`,
on the device of `flat` if the packed tensordict had a device.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(p=torch.zeros(5), v=torch.ones(5, 3), batch_size=[5])
>>> flat, layout = td.pack()
>>> out = layout.unpack(flat)
>>> assert (out == td).all()
>>> out["p"].data_ptr() == flat.data_ptr()
True
```

# PersistentTensorDict

`PersistentTensorDict` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `PersistentTensorDict` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.PersistentTensorDict(***, *batch_size=None*, *filename=None*, *group=None*, *mode='r'*, *backend='h5'*, *device=None*, *validate_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *non_tensor_as_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: `_NoShapeOps`, `_NoVmap`, `_NoSetNonTensor`, `_NoSelectExclude`, [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A tensordict whose entries live in an HDF5 file or a Zarr store.

The HDF5 backend (`backend="h5"`) needs `h5py`. The Zarr backend
(`backend="zarr"`) needs `zarr>=3.0`. Each read of an entry loads it
from the file into a new tensor, so `ptd["a"] is ptd["a"]` is
`False`, and in-place changes to the tensor that you read do not reach
the file. Writes (`ptd["a"] = value`) go to the file, and so do the
in-place methods of the tensordict, such as `ptd.add_(1)` and
`ptd.update_(other)`.

Use it to read or write existing HDF5 or Zarr data. To keep tensordict
data on disk for fast reloads, use [`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap)
instead. [Large datasets and storage backends](../../storage.html#storage) compares the storage backends, and
[Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the containers.

Open a file with [`from_h5()`](tensordict.from_h5.html#tensordict.from_h5) or [`from_zarr()`](tensordict.from_zarr.html#tensordict.from_zarr). Create one from
data with [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict). Call `close()` when you are done: the
file stays open when the object goes out of scope. To load every entry
into memory, call [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict).

Like other [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) subclasses,
`PersistentTensorDict` has a `device` attribute. This does not
mean that the data is stored on that device: the entries are cast to it
when they are read.

With the h5 backend, a string comes back as `bytes`. Starting with
TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to `str` for the strings that
tensordict wrote, which it marks with an attribute; reading one as
`bytes` warns until then. Strings that other tools wrote stay `bytes`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*or**compatible*) - the tensordict batch size.
Defaults to `torch.Size(())`.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the path to the h5 file or zarr store (for the
zarr backend, a `zarr.abc.store.Store` instance is also accepted).
Exclusive with `group`.
- **group** (*h5py.Group**or*[*Group*](https://zarr.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/zarr/group/#zarr.Group)*,**optional*) - a file or a group that
contains data. Exclusive with `filename`.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - how the file is opened, as in `h5py.File`:
`"r"` (read only), `"r+"` (read and write, the file must
exist), `"w"` (create, or truncate an existing file), `"w-"`
or `"x"` (create, fail if the file exists), `"a"` (read and
write, create the file if needed). Defaults to `"r"`.
- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - storage backend, `"h5"` (requires `h5py`) or
`"zarr"` (requires `zarr>=3.0`). Defaults to `"h5"`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible**,**optional*) - the device that the
entries are cast to when they are read. Defaults to `None`: the
entries are read on CPU and `ptd.device` is `None`.
- **validate_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size is
checked against the stored array shapes at construction time (this
requires iterating over the store metadata). Defaults to `True`.
- **non_tensor_as_stack** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a non-tensor array
that tensordict did not write, such as a string column written by
another tool, reads as a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) of its rows when its leading
dims equal the batch size, so that indexing the tensordict selects
its rows. Otherwise it reads as one
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) that holds the whole array.
Defaults to `False`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*or*[*None*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*,**optional*) - zarr non-tensor read policy.
`False` rejects pickle before decoding; `True` permits it for
trusted data. `None` (default) permits it with a `FutureWarning`
when read. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
`allow_pickle=False`. Tensor and JSON entries, and HDF5, are
unaffected.
- ****kwargs** - kwargs to be passed to `h5py.File.create_dataset()` (h5
backend) or [`zarr.Group.create_array()`](https://zarr.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/zarr/group/#zarr.Group.create_array) (zarr backend). With the
zarr backend, arrays are stored as a single chunk without compression
by default; pass `chunks=...` and/or `compressors=...` to override.

Note

PersistentTensorDict instances are not closed when they go out of
scope. Call `close()` to close the file.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import PersistentTensorDict
>>> with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as f:
... data = PersistentTensorDict(filename=f.name, batch_size=[3], mode="w")
... data["a", "b"] = torch.randn(3, 4)
... print(data)
PersistentTensorDict(
 fields={
 a: PersistentTensorDict(
 fields={
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

close()

Closes the persistent tensordict.

flatten_keys(*separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = '.'*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → T

Returns an in-memory copy where the nested keys are joined by `separator`.

The content is first loaded with [`to_tensordict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_tensordict).

Parameters:

- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the separator between the nested items. Defaults to `"."`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - must be `False`; `True` raises a `ValueError`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **is_leaf** (*callable**,**optional*) - see
[`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys).

See [`flatten_keys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.flatten_keys).

*classmethod*from_dict(*input_dict*, *filename*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *backend: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'h5'*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*)

Converts a dictionary or a TensorDict to a h5 file or zarr store.

Parameters:

- **input_dict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,*[*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*or**compatible*) - data to be stored.
- **filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**path*) - path to the h5 file or zarr store.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - not used. The batch size comes
from `batch_size`, or from the input as described there,
whatever the value of this argument
([#2247](https://github.com/pytorch/tensordict/issues/2247)). Defaults
to `False`.
- **batch_size** (*tensordict batch-size**,**optional*) - if provided, batch size
of the tensordict. If not, a tensordict input keeps its batch
size, and a dict input gets the largest leading shape that all
its entries share.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible**,**optional*) - the device where to
expect the tensor once they are returned. Defaults to `None`
(on cpu by default).
- **backend** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - storage backend, `"h5"` or `"zarr"`.
Defaults to `"h5"`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - for a dict input without
`batch_size`, the number of leading dims of the inferred
batch size. Exclusive with `batch_size`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*or*[*None*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*,**optional*) - zarr read policy for the
returned handle. `None` (default) trusts the values just
written, as does `True`. `False` rejects reads of pickled
non-tensor values. Reopening uses the new call's policy.
HDF5 is unaffected.
- ****kwargs** - kwargs to be passed to `h5py.File.create_dataset()`
(h5 backend) or [`zarr.Group.create_array()`](https://zarr.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/zarr/group/#zarr.Group.create_array) (zarr backend).

Returns:

A `PersistentTensorDict` instance linked to the newly created file.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import PersistentTensorDict
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... ptd = PersistentTensorDict.from_dict(
... {"a": torch.zeros(3, 4), "b": {"c": torch.ones(3)}},
... os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.h5"),
... )
... print(ptd.batch_size, ptd["b", "c"])
... ptd.close()
torch.Size([3]) tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

The keyword arguments that the tensordict passes to the backend when it creates a dataset.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This is internal and has no replacement.

# TensorAttrs

`TensorAttrs` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorAttrs` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorAttrs(*tgt_device: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, *tgt_dtype: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, *tgt_shape: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = None*, ***, *batch_size*, *device=None*, *names=None*)

Bases: [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass)

Per-leaf carrier describing a tensor's attributes -- device, dtype, and shape.

Mirrors the [PyTorch Tensor Attributes](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html)
terminology. Instances are produced by [`attrs()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.attrs)
-- one per leaf of the source tensordict -- and consumed by
[`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) to drive per-leaf device/dtype casting
when the source tensordict is heterogeneous (e.g. `device=None` with leaves
on different devices).

The field names are prefixed with `tgt_` to avoid shadowing the tensordict
attributes `device`/`dtype`/`shape`.

Fields populated via `from_tensor()` are controlled by the `fields` argument
so the API scales as new attributes are added.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3, device="cpu"),
... "b": torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int32)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> attrs = td.attrs()
>>> attrs["a"].tgt_device, attrs["a"].tgt_dtype
(device(type='cpu'), torch.float32)
```

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

Retrieves the device type of tensor class.

extend(*tensordict: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)] | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Appends tensordicts to the lazy stack that the instance holds.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Build a new instance with [`tensordict.lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) or
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat) instead.

*classmethod*fields() → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Field](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.Field), ...]

Returns the fields of the tensorclass.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Use `dataclasses.fields(cls)` instead. It returns the same tuple of
[`dataclasses.Field`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.Field) objects.

from_module(*as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Puts the parameters and buffers of a module in a tensordict.

The entries are the parameters and buffers of the module themselves,
not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Note

This method does not lock the result by default (`lock=False`).
The function [`tensordict.from_module()`](tensordict.from_module.html#tensordict.from_module) locks it by default
(`lock=True`).

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance is returned, which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `False`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Use it when the module has
state-dict hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no
entry. If `False`, they get an empty tensordict.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> list(params.keys())
['0']
>>> params.is_locked
False
```

*classmethod*from_tensor(*tensor*, ***, *fields=('device', 'dtype', 'shape')*)

Build a `TensorAttrs` from a tensor, populating only the requested fields.

`fields` accepts the short names `"device"`, `"dtype"`, `"shape"`. Unrequested
fields remain `None`.

*classmethod*from_tensordict(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *non_tensordict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Wraps a tensordict in a new instance of the tensorclass, without copying the leaves.

If `tensordict` is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), the entries of the fields
annotated with a tensorclass (or `Optional` of one) that are tensordicts become
instances of that tensorclass, recursively. They are set in a shallow copy of
`tensordict`, which keeps its own entries. An entry with keys that the annotated
class does not declare stays a tensordict. Other backends are wrapped as they are:
setting a tensorclass in them would write to their storage (e.g. an H5 file).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict that holds the tensor fields.
- **non_tensordict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the values of the non-tensor fields. The
fields that neither argument holds are set to `None`.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - Deprecated in 0.15, to be removed in TensorDict 0.17. Whether to
raise an error if `tensordict` is not a [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase).
Without it, such a tensordict raises an error.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Pose(TensorClass):
... q: torch.Tensor
>>> class Obs(TensorClass):
... a: Pose
>>> obs = Obs(a=Pose(q=torch.zeros(5, 4), batch_size=[5]), batch_size=[5])
>>> type(Obs.from_tensordict(obs.to_tensordict()).a).__name__
'Pose'
```

rename_keys(*mapping*, ***, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

TensorClass-specific rename_keys: the destinations must be fields, which are never removed.

select(**keys*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *strict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *as_tensordict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

TensorClass-specific select that supports `as_tensordict`.

---

# TensorClass

`TensorClass` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorClass` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorClass(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`TensorCollection`](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

A base class for dataclass-like containers of tensors.

Subclass `TensorClass` and annotate fields, as with
[`dataclasses.dataclass()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html#dataclasses.dataclass). The instances behave like a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict): they have a batch size, and they support
indexing, reshaping, `to(device)`, [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack),
[`torch.cat()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cat.html#torch.cat) and memory-mapping. A field can hold a tensor, a
tensordict, another tensorclass, or any Python object (stored as
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)). This class replaces the
[`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass) decorator, which is kept for existing code.

Use a tensorclass instead of a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) when the
data has a fixed set of named fields, when you want editors and type
checkers to know the fields, or when you want to add methods. Use a
[`TypedTensorDict`](tensordict.TypedTensorDict.html#tensordict.TypedTensorDict) instead if you need a
[`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) subclass (`state["key"]`,
`**state` unpacking). [Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the
containers, and [TensorClass](../../tensorclass.html#tensorclass-guide) is the user guide.

Examples

```
>>> from typing import Any
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... tensor: torch.Tensor
... non_tensor: Any
... nested: Any = None
>>> foo = Foo(tensor=torch.randn(3), non_tensor="a string!", nested=None, batch_size=[3])
>>> print(foo)
Foo(
 non_tensor=NonTensorData(data=a string!, batch_size=torch.Size([3]), device=None),
 tensor=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 nested=None,
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> foo[0].non_tensor
'a string!'
>>> foo.reshape(1, 3).batch_size
torch.Size([1, 3])
```

Instances support the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)
(`apply`, `reshape`, `to`, `memmap`, ...). The pages of these
methods are under [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase), because the
tensorclass forwards the call to the tensordict that holds its fields.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the instance.
Defaults to `torch.Size([])`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device of the instance. Defaults
to `None`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - The names of the batch dimensions.
Defaults to `None`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the instance is locked: writing a
field raises a `RuntimeError`. Defaults to `False`.

These keyword arguments go to the constructor, with the fields:
`Foo(tensor=..., batch_size=[3])`. The class flags below go to the
class definition instead.

Class flags

A flag changes the behavior of every instance of the class. Set it in
one of three equivalent forms:

```
>>> from tensordict import tensorclass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["autocast"]): # bracket form
... integer: int
>>> class Foo(TensorClass, autocast=True): # keyword form
... integer: int
>>> @tensorclass(autocast=True) # legacy decorator form
... class Foo:
... integer: int
```

To combine flags, list them in the brackets:

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["nocast", "frozen"]):
... integer: int
```

The flags are:

- No flag: tensor-compatible values (`int`, `float`, `np.ndarray`)
are cast to tensors. Other values are stored as
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData).

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=1).x
tensor(1)
```
- `autocast`: when a field is set, the value is converted to the
annotated type. For example, an `int` field set to
`torch.ones(())` holds `1`.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["autocast"]):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=torch.ones(())).x
1
```
- `nocast`: tensor-compatible values are stored as they are, not cast
to tensors.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["nocast"]):
... x: int
>>> Foo(x=1).x
1
```
- `tensor_only`: every field annotation must be a tensor type, a tensor
collection, or an optional or union of these. Other annotations raise
a `TypeError` when the class is defined. Values that can be cast to
a tensor (Python scalars, numpy arrays) are cast. Reading a field then
skips the lookup in the non-tensor storage.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["tensor_only"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> Foo(x=1).x
tensor(1)
```
- `frozen`: assigning a field raises `FrozenInstanceError`, as with
`@dataclass(frozen=True)`. Subclasses of a frozen class are frozen
too. A frozen class cannot subclass a non-frozen tensorclass: this
raises a `TypeError`.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["frozen"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
>>> foo.x = torch.ones(3)
Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'x'
```
- `shadow`: by default, a field whose name is a tensorclass member
(`batch_size`, `device`, `names`, `sum`, `apply` and the
other TensorDict methods) raises an `AttributeError` when the class
is defined. `shadow=True` allows these names. The field then hides
the member of the same name.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["shadow"]):
... sum: torch.Tensor
>>> Foo(sum=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3]).sum
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```
- `skip_post_init_on_rebuild`: `__post_init__` runs on the data that
comes in (the generated `__init__`, `from_tensordict`,
`from_dict`, the other constructors such as `from_any` or
`fromkeys`, and loads), but not when tensordict makes a new instance
from an existing one (indexing, `clone`, `to`, `apply`, stacking
and the other operations). Subclasses inherit the flag.

```
>>> class Foo(TensorClass["skip_post_init_on_rebuild"]):
... x: torch.Tensor
... def __post_init__(self):
... print("checked")
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
checked
>>> foo = foo.clone()
```

`autocast`, `nocast` and `tensor_only` are exclusive: combining two
of them raises a `TypeError`.

A class keyword that is not a flag, `cast_filter`, sets the default
`cast_filter` of [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to) and of the dtype
shorthands (`float()`, `bfloat16()`, ...): a predicate
`fn(key, value) -> bool` that selects the tensor leaves a dtype cast
applies to. A `cast_filter` passed to the call overrides it, and
`cast_filter=None` there casts every leaf. Subclasses inherit it. It
applies to calls on the tensorclass itself, not when the tensorclass is a
value of another tensordict or tensorclass that is cast.

```
>>> from tensordict import is_inexact
>>> class Mesh(TensorClass, cast_filter=is_inexact):
... points: torch.Tensor
... cells: torch.Tensor
>>> mesh = Mesh(points=torch.zeros(4, 3), cells=torch.zeros(2, 3, dtype=torch.long))
>>> mesh.bfloat16().points.dtype, mesh.bfloat16().cells.dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.int64)
```

Subclassing

A class with flags is a regular class. You can subclass it and add
flags:

```
>>> class Base(TensorClass["autocast"]):
... x: int
>>> class Sub(Base, shadow=True): # autocast inherited, shadow added
... y: float
```

Type checking

`TensorClass[...]` is implemented with [`__class_getitem__()`](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__class_getitem__),
so pyright resolves it to the class with flags, not to a generic
parameter. Mypy does not evaluate `__class_getitem__` in a list of base
classes and rejects the bracket form. In code that mypy checks, use the
keyword form: `class Foo(TensorClass, autocast=True)`. Editors complete
the annotated fields on instances.

Note

`TensorClass` itself is not a tensorclass: only its
subclasses become dataclasses. The reason is that a non-frozen base
cannot have a frozen subclass, and the base cannot know whether a
subclass sets `frozen`.

See also

- [`tensorclass()`](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass) for the decorator form.
- [`from_dataclass()`](tensordict.from_dataclass.html#tensordict.from_dataclass) to migrate an existing `@dataclass` to a tensorclass.
- [`TensorClassModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase) for typed `nn.Module` I/O backed by
tensorclasses.

*classmethod*from_dict(*input_dict*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *batch_dims=None*)

Builds an instance of the tensorclass from a dictionary of its fields.

The fields that `input_dict` misses are set to `None`, also those that
declare a default or a default factory. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the
default will change to filling these fields with their defaults, as the
constructor does. Until then, a call that misses such a field warns with a
[`FutureWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#FutureWarning).

Parameters:

**input_dict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) - the values of the fields. Nested dictionaries become
tensordicts, or tensorclasses for the fields annotated with one.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - whether to infer the batch size.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the batch size.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the device.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the number of batch dimensions to infer.

Wraps a tensordict in a new instance of the tensorclass, without copying the leaves.

If `tensordict` is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), the entries of the fields
annotated with a tensorclass (or `Optional` of one) that are tensordicts become

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the tensordict that holds the tensor fields.
- **non_tensordict** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - the values of the non-tensor fields. The

get(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, **args*, ***kwargs*)

Gets the value stored with the input key.

Sets a new key-value pair.

Parameters:

- **key** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,*[*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - name of the key to be set.
If tuple of str it is equivalent to chained calls of getattr
followed by a final setattr.

- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, set will tentatively try to

state_dict(*destination=None*, *prefix=''*, *keep_vars=False*, *flatten=True*) → [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

Returns a state_dict with logical keys, matching TensorDictBase conventions.

Tensor fields appear as data keys. Non-tensor fields (strings, ints, etc.)
and the tensorclass type are stored in `_metadata`. This replaces the
legacy `_tensordict`/`_non_tensordict` wrapper format.

to_tensordict(***, *retain_none: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Convert the tensorclass into a regular TensorDict.

Makes a copy of all entries. Memmap and shared memory tensors are converted to
regular tensors.

Keyword Arguments:

**retain_none** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, fields set to `None` are
written as `None` entries. Defaults to `None`, which drops
them.

Returns:

A new TensorDict object containing the same values as the tensorclass.

Examples

```
>>> from typing import Any
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass
>>> class Foo(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: Any = None
>>> foo = Foo(x=torch.zeros(3))
>>> sorted(foo.to_tensordict().keys())
['x']
>>> sorted(foo.to_tensordict(retain_none=True).keys())
['x', 'y']
```

Returns a tuple of indexed tensorclass instances unbound along the indicated dimension.

Resulting tensorclass instances will share the storage of the initial tensorclass instance.

update_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*)

Writes the entries of a dictionary, a tensordict or a tensorclass into the existing entries.

See [`update_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_). A tensorclass or dict
source ignores `keys_to_update`: the entries that it leaves out are
written too, and the call warns. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default
will change to writing only the entries in `keys_to_update`, as for a
TensorDict source.

update_at_(*input_dict_or_td: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | T*, *idx: [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [slice](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#slice) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), ...]*, *clone: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *keys_to_update: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Writes the entries of a dictionary, a tensordict or a tensorclass in place at an index.

See [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_). A tensorclass or dict
source that [`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update) accepts, such as one with the batch size of
the tensorclass, goes to [`update()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update) instead: its entries replace
those of the tensorclass whatever the index, and the call warns. Starting
with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to writing such a source in
place at the index, as [`update_at_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_at_)
does.

# TensorCollection

*class*tensordict.TensorCollection(**args*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A base class for TensorDictBase and TensorClass.

This is an abstract base class that provides the foundation for tensor collections
like TensorDict and TensorClass. It serves as a common interface for all tensor
collection types in the tensordict library.

Use it in type hints and `isinstance` checks for "a tensordict or a
tensorclass". Classes decorated with `@tensorclass` do not inherit from
it, only subclasses of [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) do; to check both,
use [`is_tensor_collection()`](tensordict.is_tensor_collection.html#tensordict.is_tensor_collection).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorClass, TensorCollection, TensorDict
>>> class Data(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> isinstance(td, TensorCollection)
True
>>> isinstance(Data(x=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]), TensorCollection)
True
>>> isinstance(torch.zeros(3), TensorCollection)
False
```

# TensorDict

`TensorDict` has the methods of [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase),
listed by task in [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods). This page lists only the
methods that `TensorDict` adds, and the overrides that have their own
documentation.

*class*tensordict.TensorDict(*source: T | [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*)

Bases: [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

A dictionary of tensors that share a batch size.

The batch size is the leading part of the shape that every entry has in
common. With `batch_size=[3, 4]`, every entry has a shape that starts
with `(3, 4)`. Shape operations (indexing, `reshape`, `view`,
`unsqueeze`, `permute`, masking) act on the batch dimensions of every
entry at once. Pointwise operations (`td + other`, `td * 2`),
`td.to(device)` and `td.to(dtype)` apply to every entry. An entry can
be another tensordict, so keys can be nested: `td["a", "b"]` reads the
entry `"b"` of the nested tensordict `"a"`. [Batch size, shapes, and indexing](../../concepts/batch_size.html#batch-size) and
[Keys, nested keys, and locking](../../concepts/keys.html#keys) explain these ideas.

Use `TensorDict` for most data. To stack tensordicts whose keys or
entry shapes differ, use [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict). To
declare a fixed set of fields with types, use
[`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) or [`TypedTensorDict`](tensordict.TypedTensorDict.html#tensordict.TypedTensorDict).
[Which container should I use?](../../choosing_a_container.html#choosing-a-container) compares the containers.

Build a tensordict from a dict, or from keyword arguments as with
`dict(...)`:

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {"obs": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5), "reward": torch.zeros(3, 4)},
... batch_size=[3, 4],
... )
>>> td[0]["obs"].shape
torch.Size([4, 5])
>>> td.view(-1)["obs"].shape
torch.Size([12, 5])
>>> (td + 1)["reward"].sum()
tensor(12.)
>>> td.to(torch.float64)["obs"].dtype
torch.float64
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> td["b", "c"].shape
torch.Size([3, 2])
```

A tensordict has these constraints:

- The batch size is not inferred from the data: it defaults to `[]`.
Call [`auto_batch_size_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_) to set it to
the largest leading shape that all entries share.
- The shape of every entry must start with the batch size. If it does
not, setting the entry raises a `RuntimeError`.
- If `device` is set, every entry is moved to that device. If it is
not set, the entries can be on different devices.
- A key is a string, or a tuple of strings for a nested entry.

Parameters:

- **source** (*TensorDict**or**Mapping**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**Union**[**Tensor**,*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*]**]*) - a
data source, such as a `dict` or any other
[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping), read like a `dict`. If empty,
the tensordict can be populated subsequently.
A `TensorDict` can also be built via a sequence of keyword arguments,
as it is the case for `dict(...)`.
- **batch_size** (*iterable**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - a batch size for the
tensordict. The batch size can be modified subsequently as long
as it is compatible with its content.
If no batch size is provided, an empty batch size is assumed (it
is not inferred automatically from the data). To automatically set
the batch size, refer to [`auto_batch_size_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_).
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible type**,**optional*) - a device for the
TensorDict. If provided, all tensors will be stored on that device.
If not, tensors on different devices are allowed.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the names of the dimensions of the
tensordict. If provided, its length must match the one of the
`batch_size`. Defaults to `None` (no dimension name, or `None`
for every dimension).
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and a device is passed, the
entries are moved to the device without synchronization. This is
safe only from CPU to CUDA. In other cases, you must synchronize
yourself. If `False`, every move is synchronous. If `None`
(default), the moves are asynchronous, and the constructor
synchronizes after them if required.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict will be
locked.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> source = {'random': torch.randn(3, 4),
... 'zeros': torch.zeros(3, 4, 5)}
>>> batch_size = [3]
>>> td = TensorDict(source, batch_size=batch_size)
>>> print(td.shape) # equivalent to td.batch_size
torch.Size([3])
>>> td_unsqueeze = td.unsqueeze(-1)
>>> print(td_unsqueeze.get("zeros").shape)
torch.Size([3, 1, 4, 5])
>>> print(td_unsqueeze[0].shape)
torch.Size([1])
>>> print(td_unsqueeze.view(-1).shape)
torch.Size([3])
>>> print((td.clone()==td).all())
True
>>> td_add = td.apply(lambda x, y: x + y, td)
>>> (td_add["random"] == 2 * td["random"]).all()
tensor(True)
```

*classmethod*from_module(*module: [Module](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Puts the parameters and buffers of a module in a tensordict.

The entries are the parameters and buffers of the module themselves,
not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Note

This method does not lock the result by default (`lock=False`).
The function [`tensordict.from_module()`](tensordict.from_module.html#tensordict.from_module) locks it by default
(`lock=True`).

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance is returned, which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `False`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Use it when the module has
state-dict hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no
entry. If `False`, they get an empty tensordict.
Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

a `TensorDict`, or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> list(params.keys())
['0']
>>> params.is_locked
False
```

# TensorDictBase.__getitem__

TensorDictBase.__getitem__(*index: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*) → Any

TensorDictBase.__getitem__(*index: IndexType*) → Self

Indexes all tensors according to the provided index.

The index can be a (nested) key or any valid shape index given the
tensordict batch size.

If the index is a nested key and the result is a [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)
object, the content of the non-tensor is returned.

Examples

```
>>> td = TensorDict({"root": torch.arange(2), ("nested", "entry"): torch.arange(2)}, [2])
>>> td["root"]
tensor([0, 1])
>>> td["nested", "entry"]
tensor([0, 1])
>>> td[:1]
TensorDict(
 fields={
 nested: TensorDict(
 fields={
 entry: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([1]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False),
 root: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([1]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.add

TensorDictBase.add(*other: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, ***, *alpha: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *default: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Adds `other`, scaled by `alpha`, to `self`.

\[\text{out}_i = \text{input}_i + \text{alpha} \times \text{other}_i\]

Parameters:

**other** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the tensor or TensorDict to add to `self`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **alpha** (*Number**,**optional*) - the multiplier for `other`.
- **default** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the value to use for an
entry that only one of the two tensordicts has. If `None`
(default), the two tensordicts must have the same keys, and a
missing key raises `KeyError`. If `"intersection"`, only
the keys that both tensordicts have are computed, and the
other keys are dropped. Any other value replaces the missing
entries on both sides of the operation.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.apply

TensorDictBase.apply(*fn: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)*, **others: T*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = NO_DEFAULT*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *default: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = NO_DEFAULT*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *propagate_lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *call_on_nested: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *is_leaf: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***constructor_kwargs*) → Self | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Applies a callable to all values stored in the tensordict and sets them in a new tensordict.

The callable signature must be `Callable[Tuple[Tensor, ...], Tensor | TensorDictBase | None]`.

Parameters:

- **fn** (*Callable*) - function to be applied to the tensors in the
tensordict.
- ***others** (*TensorDictBase instances**,**optional*) - if provided, these
tensordict instances should have a structure matching the one
of self. The `fn` argument should receive as many
unnamed inputs as the number of tensordicts, including self.
If other tensordicts have missing entries, a default value
can be passed through the `default` keyword argument.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** (*sequence**of*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - if provided,
the resulting TensorDict will have the desired batch_size.
The [`batch_size`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.batch_size.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.batch_size) argument should match the batch_size after
the transformation. This is a keyword only argument.
With a `batch_size`, the call is treated as a shape operation:
`fn` is not called on [`UnbatchedTensor`](tensordict.UnbatchedTensor.html#tensordict.UnbatchedTensor)
entries, which keep their data and take the new batch size.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the resulting device, if any.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the new dimension names, in case the
batch_size is modified.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the results are written into
the existing leaves of `self` (as [`set_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_) does), and
`self` is returned. Defaults to `False`. See
[In-place operations](../../concepts/operations.html#inplace-conventions).
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - default value for missing entries in the
other tensordicts. If not provided, missing entries will
raise a KeyError.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, empty tensordicts will be
filtered out. This also comes with a lower computational cost as
empty data structures won't be created and destroyed. Non-tensor data
is considered as a leaf and thereby will be kept in the tensordict even
if left untouched by the function. If `False`, empty tensordicts are kept.
Defaults to `None`, which behaves like `True` (tensordicts left empty by
`fn` are filtered out, and `None` is returned if `fn` returns no value at
all) except that tensordicts that were already empty are kept.
- **propagate_lock** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a locked tensordict will produce
another locked tensordict. Defaults to `False`.
- **call_on_nested** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, the function will be called on first-level tensors
and containers (TensorDict or tensorclass). In this scenario, `func` is responsible of
propagating its calls to nested levels. This allows a fine-grained behaviour
when propagating the calls to nested tensordicts.
If `False`, the function will only be called on leaves, and `apply` will take care of dispatching
the function to all leaves.

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, is_tensor_collection
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": {"b": [0.0, 1.0]}, "c": [1.0, 2.0]})
>>> def mean_tensor_only(val):
... if is_tensor_collection(val):
... raise RuntimeError("Unexpected!")
... return val.mean()
>>> td_mean = td.apply(mean_tensor_only)
>>> def mean_any(val):
... if is_tensor_collection(val):
... # Recurse
... return val.apply(mean_any, call_on_nested=True)
... return val.mean()
>>> td_mean = td.apply(mean_any, call_on_nested=True)
```
- **is_leaf** (*Callable**[**[*[*type*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.type.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.type)*]**,*[*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*]**,**optional*) - 

called with the type of
each entry; `fn` is called on the entries for which it returns
`True`, and `apply` goes into the others. Defaults to `None`,
which uses [`default_is_leaf()`](tensordict.default_is_leaf.html#tensordict.default_is_leaf): `fn` is called
on tensors, and `apply` goes into tensordicts, tensorclasses
and non-tensor data (which is kept unchanged). Pass
[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor) to call `fn` on non-tensor
data too:

```
>>> from tensordict import is_leaf_nontensor
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b="a string", batch_size=[3])
>>> seen = []
>>> _ = td.apply(lambda x: seen.append(type(x).__name__))
>>> seen
['Tensor']
>>> seen = []
>>> _ = td.apply(lambda x: seen.append(type(x).__name__), is_leaf=is_leaf_nontensor)
>>> seen
['Tensor', 'NonTensorData']
```
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - 

a tensordict where to write the results. This can be used to avoid
creating a new tensordict:

```
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": 0})
>>> _ = td.apply(lambda x: x+1, out=td)
>>> assert (td==1).all()
```

Warning

If the operation executed on the tensordict requires multiple keys to be accessed for
a single computation, providing an `out` argument equal to `self` can cause the operation
to provide silently wrong results.
For instance:

```
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": 1, "b": 1})
>>> td.apply(lambda x: x+td["a"])["b"] # Right!
tensor(2)
>>> td.apply(lambda x: x+td["a"], out=td)["b"] # Wrong!
tensor(3)
```
- ****constructor_kwargs** - additional keyword arguments to be passed to the
TensorDict constructor.

Returns:

a new tensordict with the transformed tensors, or `self` if
`inplace=True`. `None` if `fn` returns `None` for every
leaf and `filter_empty` is not `False`.

The result has the same type as `self` for
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict),
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) and tensorclasses.
Other types, for example
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict) or a memory-mapped
tensordict, give a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) that lives in
memory.

A locked tensordict gives an unlocked result unless
`propagate_lock=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({
... "a": -torch.ones(3),
... "b": {"c": torch.ones(3)}},
... batch_size=[3])
>>> td_1 = td.apply(lambda x: x+1)
>>> assert (td_1["a"] == 0).all()
>>> assert (td_1["b", "c"] == 2).all()
>>> td_2 = td.apply(lambda x, y: x+y, td)
>>> assert (td_2["a"] == -2).all()
>>> assert (td_2["b", "c"] == 2).all()
```

Note

If `None` is returned by the function, the entry is ignored. This
can be used to filter the data in the tensordict:

```
>>> td = TensorDict({"1": 1, "2": 2, "b": {"2": 2, "1": 1}}, [])
>>> def filter(tensor):
... if tensor == 1:
... return tensor
>>> td.apply(filter)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
