# TensorDictBase.from_dict

*abstract classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_dict(*input_dict*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Returns a TensorDict created from a dictionary or another [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

If `batch_size` is not specified and `auto_batch_size=True`, the maximum batch size possible is used.

This function works on nested dictionaries too. For [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), a tensor
collection passed as `input_dict` is currently returned as is, and the keyword arguments are
not applied to it: use [`auto_batch_size_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.auto_batch_size_) to compute the batch size of an existing
tensordict.

Parameters:

**input_dict** (*dictionary**,**optional*) - a dictionary to use as a data source
(nested keys compatible).

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically.
Defaults to `None`, which behaves like `False`, unless
`batch_dims` is passed: then it behaves like `True`.
- **batch_size** (*iterable**of*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - a batch size for the tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible type**,**optional*) - a device for the TensorDict.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the maximum number of leading dimensions
of the computed batch size. A smaller number is used if the
tensors do not share that many leading dimensions. Exclusive
with `batch_size`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the dimension names of the tensordict.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3, 4), "b": torch.randn(3)}
>>> print(TensorDict.from_dict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # nested dict: the nested TensorDict can have a different batch-size
>>> # as long as its leading dims match.
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}
>>> print(TensorDict.from_dict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # to work out the batch size of an existing tensordict, use auto_batch_size_
>>> input_td = TensorDict({"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}, [])
>>> print(input_td.auto_batch_size_())
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_dict_instance

TensorDictBase.from_dict_instance(*input_dict*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size=None*, *device=None*, *batch_dims=None*, *names=None*)

Instance method version of [`from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict).

Unlike [`from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict), this method will
attempt to keep the tensordict types within the existing tree (for
any existing leaf).

Examples

```

... class MyClass:
... x: torch.Tensor
... y: int

>>> print(td.from_dict_instance(td.to_dict()))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: MyClass(
 x=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(td.from_dict(td.to_dict()))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# TensorDictBase.from_h5

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_h5(*filename*, ***, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'r'*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_tensor_as_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Creates a PersistentTensorDict from a h5 file.

Parameters:

**filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - The path to the h5 file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - how the file is opened: `"r"` (read only),
`"r+"` (read and write), or another mode of `h5py.File`
(see [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict)). Defaults to `"r"`.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically.
Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If auto_batch_size is `True`, defines how many dimensions the output
tensordict should have. Defaults to `None` (full batch-size at each level).
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the TensorDict. Defaults to `None`.
- **non_tensor_as_stack** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a non-tensor
dataset that tensordict did not write, such as a string column
with one string per row, reads as a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) of its rows when its
leading dims equal the batch size. Otherwise it reads as one
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) that holds the whole
dataset. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A PersistentTensorDict representation of the input h5 file.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict(key1=torch.zeros(3), key2=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "file.h5")
... _ = data.to_h5(path)
... td = TensorDict.from_h5(path)
... print(td)
PersistentTensorDict(
 fields={
 key1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 key2: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_json

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_json(*path*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lines: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Creates a TensorDict from a JSON file.

Supports both standard JSON (array of records) and JSON Lines format.
For nested JSON objects, use [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict) instead.

Requires pandas for best results. Falls back to stdlib `json`
for simple cases.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - Path to the JSON file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the batch size will
be computed automatically. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If `auto_batch_size` is `True`,
defines how many dimensions the output tensordict should have.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device for tensor data.
Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size. Defaults to
`[num_rows]`.
- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - If provided, column names are split on
this separator to create nested TensorDicts. Defaults to `None`.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - If provided, all numeric columns
are cast to this dtype. Defaults to `None`.
- **lines** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, reads the file as JSON Lines
(one JSON object per line). Defaults to `False`.
- ****kwargs** - Additional keyword arguments forwarded to the JSON
reader.

Returns:

A TensorDict representation of the JSON data.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict(obs=torch.arange(3.0), reward=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.json")
... data.to_json(path)
... td = TensorDict.from_json(path)
... path_lines = os.path.join(tmpdir, "data.jsonl")
... data.to_json(path_lines, lines=True)
... td_lines = TensorDict.from_json(path_lines, lines=True)
>>> td.batch_size, td_lines.batch_size
(torch.Size([3]), torch.Size([3]))
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_list

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_list(*input*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *lazy: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Builds a tensordict by stacking a list of dicts or tensor collections.

Each dict is converted with [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict) and the results are
stacked along a new leading dimension.

Parameters:

**input** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)) - the dicts or tensor collections to stack.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size of
each element is computed automatically. See [`from_dict()`](tensordict.from_dict.html#tensordict.from_dict).
- **batch_size** (*iterable**of*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the batch size of the
result, with the length of the list first. Each element gets
`batch_size[1:]`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible type**,**optional*) - a device for
the result.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the maximum number of batch dimensions
of the result, the list dimension included. Exclusive with
`batch_size`.
- **names** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the dimension names of the result,
one per batch dimension, with the name of the list dimension
first.
- **lazy** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the result is a lazy stack;
if `False`, a dense stack. Defaults to `None`, which builds
a dense stack when the elements have the same shape and a lazy
stack otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict.from_list(
... [{"a": torch.zeros(3)}, {"a": torch.zeros(3)}],
... batch_size=[2, 3],
... names=["x", "y"],
... )
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2, 3])
>>> td.names
['x', 'y']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_module

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_module(*module*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Returns a tensordict of the parameters and buffers of a module.

The leaves are the parameters and buffers of the module, not copies:
an in-place change to a leaf changes the module. Use
`TensorDict.from_module(module).data.clone()` to get independent
tensors. Submodules become sub-tensordicts: `module.layers[0].weight`
is the entry `("layers", "0", "weight")`. Write the parameters back
with [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module).

The result is a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or a
`TensorDictParams` with `as_module=True`),
whichever class this method is called on.

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance will be returned which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict will be locked.
Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, the state-dict from the
module will be used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Defaults to `False`.

Note

This is particularly useful when state-dict hooks have to be used.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from torch import nn
>>> module = nn.TransformerDecoder(
... decoder_layer=nn.TransformerDecoderLayer(nhead=4, d_model=4),
... num_layers=1
... )
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> print(params["layers", "0", "linear1"])
TensorDict(
 fields={
 bias: Parameter(shape=torch.Size([2048]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 weight: Parameter(shape=torch.Size([2048, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_modules

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_modules(**modules*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lazy_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *expand_identical: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Retrieves the parameters of several modules for ensebmle learning/feature of expects applications through vmap.

Parameters:

**modules** (*sequence**of**nn.Module*) - the modules to get the parameters from.
If the modules differ in their structure, a lazy stack is needed
(see the `lazy_stack` argument below).

Keyword Arguments:

- **as_module** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a `TensorDictParams`
instance will be returned which can be used to store parameters
within a [`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict will be locked.
Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - 

if `True`, the state-dict from the
module will be used and unflattened into a TensorDict with
the tree structure of the model. Defaults to `False`.

Note

This is particularly useful when state-dict hooks have to be used.
- **lazy_stack** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - 

whether parameters should be densly or
lazily stacked. Defaults to `False` (dense stack).

Note

`lazy_stack` and `as_module` are exclusive features.

Warning

There is a crucial difference between lazy and non-lazy outputs
in that non-lazy output will reinstantiate parameters with the
desired batch-size, while `lazy_stack` will just represent
the parameters as lazily stacked. This means that whilst the
original parameters can safely be passed to an optimizer
when `lazy_stack=True`, the new parameters need to be passed
when it is set to `True`.

Warning

Whilst it can be tempting to use a lazy stack to keep the
orignal parameter references, remember that lazy stack
perform a stack each time [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) is called. This will
require memory (N times the size of the parameters, more if a
graph is built) and time to be computed.
It also means that the optimizer(s) will contain more
parameters, and operations like [`step()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.Optimizer.step.html#torch.optim.Optimizer.step)
or [`zero_grad()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.Optimizer.zero_grad.html#torch.optim.Optimizer.zero_grad) will take longer
to be executed. In general, `lazy_stack` should be reserved
to very few use cases.
- **expand_identical** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and the same parameter (same
identity) is being stacked to itself, an expanded version of this parameter
will be returned instead. This argument is ignored when `lazy_stack=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> empty_module = nn.Linear(3, 4, device="meta")
>>> n_models = 2
>>> modules = [nn.Linear(3, 4) for _ in range(n_models)]
>>> params = TensorDict.from_modules(*modules)
>>> print(params)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 bias: Parameter(shape=torch.Size([2, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 weight: Parameter(shape=torch.Size([2, 4, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # example of batch execution
>>> def exec_module(params, x):
... with params.to_module(empty_module):
... return empty_module(x)
>>> x = torch.randn(3)
>>> y = torch.vmap(exec_module, (0, None))(params, x)
>>> assert y.shape == (n_models, 4)
>>> # since lazy_stack = False, backprop leaves the original params untouched
>>> y.sum().backward()
>>> assert params["weight"].grad.norm() > 0
>>> assert modules[0].weight.grad is None
```

With `lazy_stack=True`, things are slightly different:

```
>>> params = TensorDict.from_modules(*modules, lazy_stack=True)
>>> print(params)
LazyStackedTensorDict(
 fields={
 bias: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 weight: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 4, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 exclusive_fields={
 },
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False,
 stack_dim=0)
>>> # example of batch execution
>>> y = torch.vmap(exec_module, (0, None))(params, x)
>>> assert y.shape == (n_models, 4)
>>> y.sum().backward()
>>> assert modules[0].weight.grad is not None
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_namedtuple(*named_tuple*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Converts a namedtuple to a TensorDict recursively.

Parameters:

**named_tuple** - The namedtuple instance to be converted.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically.
Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If `auto_batch_size` is `True`, defines how many dimensions the output
tensordict should have. Defaults to `None` (full batch-size at each level).
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device on which the TensorDict will be created.
Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the TensorDict.
Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

A TensorDict representation of the input namedtuple.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> import torch
>>> data = TensorDict({
... "a_tensor": torch.zeros((3)),
... "nested": {"a_tensor": torch.zeros((3)), "a_string": "zero!"}}, [3])
>>> nt = data.to_namedtuple()
>>> print(nt)
GenericDict(a_tensor=tensor([0., 0., 0.]), nested=GenericDict(a_tensor=tensor([0., 0., 0.]), a_string='zero!'))
>>> TensorDict.from_namedtuple(nt, auto_batch_size=True)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a_tensor: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 nested: TensorDict(
 fields={
 a_string: NonTensorData(data=zero!, batch_size=torch.Size([3]), device=None),
 a_tensor: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# TensorDictBase.from_parquet

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_parquet(*path*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *separator: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *dtype: [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *columns: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → Self

Creates a TensorDict from a Parquet file.

Requires either pyarrow or pandas to be installed. Prefers pyarrow
when available for better performance.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - Path to the Parquet file.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the batch size will
be computed automatically. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If `auto_batch_size` is `True`,
defines how many dimensions the output tensordict should have.
Defaults to `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device for tensor data.
Defaults to `None`.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size. Defaults to
`[num_rows]`.
- **separator** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - If provided, column names are split on
this separator to create nested TensorDicts. Defaults to `None`.
- **dtype** ([*dtype*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)*,**optional*) - If provided, all numeric columns
are cast to this dtype. Defaults to `None`.
- **columns** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - If provided, only read these
columns from the file. Defaults to `None` (all columns).
- ****kwargs** - Additional keyword arguments forwarded to the Parquet
reader.

A TensorDict representation of the Parquet data.

Examples

```
>>> import os

... td = TensorDict.from_parquet(path)
... td_obs = TensorDict.from_parquet(path, columns=["obs"])
>>> sorted(td.keys()), sorted(td_obs.keys())

# TensorDictBase.from_pytree

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_pytree(*pytree*, ***, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Converts a pytree to a TensorDict instance.

This method is designed to keep the pytree nested structure as much as possible.

Additional non-tensor keys are added to keep track of each level's identity, providing
a built-in pytree-to-tensordict bijective transform API.

Accepted classes currently include lists, tuples, named tuples and dict,
and subclasses of these such as [`collections.OrderedDict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.OrderedDict),
[`collections.defaultdict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.defaultdict) and the results of `torch.max` and
the other `torch.return_types`. A `defaultdict` is rebuilt without
its `default_factory`.

Note

For dictionaries, non-NestedKey keys are registered separately as [`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)
instances.

Note

Tensor-castable types (such as int, float or np.ndarray) will be converted to torch.Tensor instances.
Note that this transformation is surjective: transforming back the tensordict to a pytree will not
recover the original types.

Note

A module `state_dict()` round-trips through `from_pytree`, and its
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap) output loads with `load_memmap(path, allow_pickle=False)`.
The state dicts of an optimizer and of a learning-rate scheduler hold
`None`, `str` values and Python numbers, which `from_pytree` rejects
(`None` and `str`) or returns as tensors (numbers): save them with
`torch.save(sd, path)` and load them with `torch.load(path, weights_only=True)`,
which round-trips them exactly without unpickling arbitrary objects.

Note

The list fields of a named tuple, and some of its dict and tuple
fields, are converted with [`from_any()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_any.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_any) and do not
round-trip through [`to_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree):

- a list of numbers comes back as a tensor;
- a dict holding a str, list or tuple, and an empty dict or named
tuple (or a dict or named tuple holding one), come back as a
`GenericDict` named tuple;
- a tuple subclass, such as a `torch.return_types` result, and
a plain tuple holding anything but tensors, Python ints and
floats, dicts and named tuples (such as a str, a list or a NumPy
number), or holding one of the dicts or named tuples above, make
[`to_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree) raise a `ValueError`, and an empty tuple
comes back as an empty `GenericDict`.

The other dict, named tuple and plain tuple fields come back with
their own type.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> # Create a pytree with tensor leaves, and one "weird"-looking dict key
>>> class WeirdLookingClass:
... pass
...
>>> weird_key = WeirdLookingClass()
>>> # Make a pytree with tuple, lists, dict and namedtuple
>>> pytree = (
... [torch.randint(10, (3,)), torch.zeros(2)],
... {
... "tensor": torch.randn(
... 2,
... ),
... "td": TensorDict({"one": 1}),
... weird_key: torch.randint(10, (2,)),
... "list": [1, 2, 3],
... },
... {"named_tuple": TensorDict({"two": torch.ones(1) * 2}).to_namedtuple()},
... )
>>> # Build a TensorDict from that pytree
>>> td = TensorDict.from_pytree(pytree)
>>> # Recover the pytree
>>> pytree_recon = td.to_pytree()
>>> # Check that the leaves match
>>> def check(v1, v2):
... assert (v1 == v2).all()
...
>>> _ = torch.utils._pytree.tree_map(check, pytree, pytree_recon)
>>> assert weird_key in pytree_recon[1]
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_remote_init

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_remote_init(*src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *group: 'ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *use_broadcast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Creates a new tensordict instance initialized from remotely sent metadata.

This class method receives consolidated metadata and a single storage buffer
sent by [`init_remote()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.init_remote.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.init_remote), then reconstructs the full tensordict.

Two transport modes are available (must match the sender's choice):

- **Point-to-point** (default): uses `recv_object_list` +
`dist.recv`. Only sender and receiver participate.
- **Broadcast** (`use_broadcast=True`): delegates to
[`broadcast()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast). All ranks must participate.

Parameters:

- **src** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - The rank of the source process that sent the metadata.
- **group** (*"ProcessGroup"**,**optional*) - The process group to use for communication. Defaults to None.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device to use for tensor operations. Defaults to None.
- **use_broadcast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - If `True`, use [`broadcast()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast) instead
of point-to-point recv. Must match the sender's setting.
Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

A new tensordict instance initialized with the received metadata and content.

Return type:

[*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

See also

The sending process should have called ~.init_remote to send the metadata and content.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_schema

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_schema(*schema: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size), [dtype](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.dtype)]]*, ***, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *storage: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device=None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Pre-allocate a zero-filled TensorDict from a schema.

Creates a [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) whose storage backend is selected
by `storage`. Each entry in `schema` maps a field name to an
`(element_shape, dtype)` pair; the full stored shape is
`[*batch_size, *element_shape]`.

Parameters:

**schema** - Mapping from field name to `(element_shape, dtype)`.
`element_shape` is the per-element shape (excluding
`batch_size`).

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** - Overall batch dimensions prepended to every element
shape. Defaults to `()`.
- **storage** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*None*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) - 

Backend selector:

- `None` - plain [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with regular tensors.
- `"memmap"` - memory-mapped tensors on disk.
Pass `prefix=<dir>` in *kwargs*.
- `"h5"` - HDF5 via [`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict).
Pass `filename=<path>` in *kwargs*.
- `"zarr"` - zarr (requires `zarr>=3.0`) via
[`PersistentTensorDict`](tensordict.PersistentTensorDict.html#tensordict.PersistentTensorDict). Pass `filename=<path or store>`
in *kwargs*.
- `"shared"` - CPU shared-memory tensors.
- `"redis"` / `"dragonfly"` - delegates to
`TensorDictStore.from_schema()`.
- **device** - Device for the resulting tensors (ignored by some
backends).
- ****kwargs** - Backend-specific arguments forwarded to the
underlying constructor (e.g. `prefix` for memmap,
`filename` for h5, `host`/`port` for redis).

Returns:

A new [`TensorDictBase`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) subclass instance with
pre-allocated (zero-filled) keys.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict.from_schema(
... {"obs": ([84, 84, 3], torch.uint8),
... "reward": ([], torch.float32)},
... batch_size=[1000],
... )
>>> td["obs"].shape
torch.Size([1000, 84, 84, 3])
```

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
... td_mm = TensorDict.from_schema(
... {"obs": ([4], torch.float32)},
... batch_size=[8],
... storage="memmap",
... prefix=d,
... )
... assert td_mm.is_memmap()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_struct_array

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_struct_array(*struct_array: [ndarray](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray)*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self

Converts a structured numpy array to a TensorDict.

The resulting TensorDict will share the same memory content as the numpy array (it is a zero-copy operation).
Changing values of the structured numpy array in-place will affect the content of the TensorDict.

Note

This method performs a zero-copy operation, meaning that the resulting TensorDict will share the same memory
content as the input numpy array. Therefore, changing values of the numpy array in-place will affect the content
of the TensorDict.
The exception is a field whose item size does not divide the size of a record, such as the `"i8"`
field of a packed array of `"i8"` and `"f4"` fields (12 bytes per record): torch cannot view such a
field, so it is copied.

Parameters:

**struct_array** (*np.ndarray*) - The structured numpy array to be converted.

Keyword Arguments:

- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If `auto_batch_size` is `True`, defines how many dimensions the output
tensordict should have. Defaults to `None` (full batch-size at each level).
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - 

The device on which the TensorDict will be created.
Defaults to `None`.

Note

Changing the device (i.e., specifying any device other than `None` or `"cpu"`) will transfer the data,
resulting in a change to the memory location of the returned data.
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the TensorDict. Defaults to None.

Returns:

A TensorDict representation of the input structured numpy array.

Examples

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> x = np.array(
... [("Rex", 9, 81.0), ("Fido", 3, 27.0)],
... dtype=[("name", "U10"), ("age", "i4"), ("weight", "f4")],
... )
>>> td = TensorDict.from_struct_array(x)
>>> x_recon = td.to_struct_array()
>>> assert (x_recon == x).all()
>>> assert x_recon.shape == x.shape
>>> # Try modifying x age field and check effect on td
>>> x["age"] += 1
>>> assert (td["age"] == np.array([10, 4])).all()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.from_tuple

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_tuple(*obj*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

# TensorDictBase.from_zarr

*classmethod*TensorDictBase.from_zarr(*filename*, ***, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'r'*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_tensor_as_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Creates a PersistentTensorDict from a zarr store.

Requires `zarr>=3.0` to be installed.

Parameters:

**filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**path**or**zarr store*) - The path to the zarr store (a
directory), or a `zarr.abc.store.Store` instance (e.g. a
`zarr.storage.ZipStore`).

Keyword Arguments:

- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - Reading mode. Defaults to `"r"`.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically.
Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If auto_batch_size is `True`, defines how many dimensions the output
tensordict should have. Defaults to `None` (full batch-size at each level).
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the TensorDict. Defaults to `None`
(read from the metadata written by [`to_zarr()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_zarr.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_zarr), or automatically determined
for stores written by other tools).
- **non_tensor_as_stack** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a non-tensor
array that tensordict did not write, such as a string column
with one string per row, reads as a
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack) of its rows when its
leading dims equal the batch size. Otherwise it reads as one
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) that holds the whole
array. Defaults to `False`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*or*[*None*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*,**optional*) - whether to decode pickled
non-tensor values. `False` rejects them before decoding;
`True` permits them only for data you trust. The default,
`None`, permits them with a `FutureWarning` when read.
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to
`allow_pickle=False`. Tensor and JSON entries are unaffected.

Returns:

A PersistentTensorDict representation of the input zarr store.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict(key1=torch.zeros(3), key2=torch.ones(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "store.zarr")
... _ = data.to_zarr(path)
... td = TensorDict.from_zarr(path)
... print(td)
PersistentTensorDict(
 fields={
 key1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 key2: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.gather

TensorDictBase.gather(*dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *index: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → Self

Gathers values along an axis specified by dim.

Parameters:

- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the dimension along which collect the elements
- **index** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - a long tensor which number of dimension matches
the one of the tensordict with only one dimension differing between
the two (the gathering dimension). Its elements refer to the
index to be gathered along the required dimension.
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a destination tensordict. It must
have the same shape as the index.

Keyword Arguments:

**inplace** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, this tensordict's identity
and key set are preserved; each leaf storage is replaced by
its gathered counterpart one leaf at a time, keeping peak
memory close to `1x`. Requires `index.ndim ==
self.batch_dims` (the result must have the same number of
batch dims as the input). Mutually exclusive with `out`.
Not supported on [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).
Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {"a": torch.randn(3, 4, 5),
... "b": TensorDict({"c": torch.zeros(3, 4, 5)}, [3, 4, 5])},
... [3, 4])
>>> index = torch.randint(4, (3, 2))
>>> td_gather = td.gather(dim=1, index=index)
>>> print(td_gather)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 2, 5]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 2, 5]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 2, 5]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Gather keeps the dimension names.

Examples

```
>>> td.names = ["a", "b"]
>>> td_gather = td.gather(dim=1, index=index)
>>> td_gather.names
['a', 'b']
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.gather_and_stack

TensorDictBase.gather_and_stack(*dst: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → Self | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Gathers tensordicts from various workers and stacks them onto self in the destination worker.

Parameters:

- **dst** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - the rank of the destination worker where `gather_and_stack()` will be called.
- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - if set, the specified process group
will be used for communication. Otherwise, the default process group
will be used.
Defaults to `None`.

Example

```
>>> from torch import multiprocessing as mp
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> def client():
... torch.distributed.init_process_group(
... "gloo",
... rank=1,
... world_size=2,
... init_method=f"tcp://localhost:10003",
... )
... # Create a single tensordict to be sent to server
... td = TensorDict(
... {("a", "b"): torch.randn(2),
... "c": torch.randn(2)}, [2]
... )
... td.gather_and_stack(0)
...
>>> def server():
... torch.distributed.init_process_group(
... "gloo",
... rank=0,
... world_size=2,
... init_method=f"tcp://localhost:10003",
... )
... # Creates the destination tensordict on server.
... # The first dim must be equal to world_size-1
... td = TensorDict(
... {("a", "b"): torch.zeros(2),
... "c": torch.zeros(2)}, [2]
... ).expand(1, 2).contiguous()
... td.gather_and_stack(0)
... assert td["a", "b"] != 0
... print("yuppie")
...
>>> if __name__ == "__main__":
... mp.set_start_method("spawn")
...
... main_worker = mp.Process(target=server)
... secondary_worker = mp.Process(target=client)
...
... main_worker.start()
... secondary_worker.start()
...
... main_worker.join()
... secondary_worker.join()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.get

TensorDictBase.get(*key*)

TensorDictBase.get(*key*, *default*)

Returns the value stored at `key`, or `default` if the key is missing.

`td.get(key)` is the same as `td[key]`, except for a missing key:
`td[key]` raises `KeyError`, and `get` returns `default`.

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key to read. A tuple reads a nested entry:
`td.get(("a", "b"))` is `td["a"]["b"]`. See [Keys, nested keys, and locking](../../concepts/keys.html#keys).
- **default** (*optional*) - the value returned if the key is missing.
Defaults to `None`, as for [`dict.get()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict.get). A nested key
that runs through a tensor is missing too: `get` returns
the default passed to it, and without one raises a
`ValueError` that names the tensor.

Changed in version 0.7: A missing key returns `None` instead of raising `KeyError`.
`set_get_defaults_to_none(False)` and `TD_GET_DEFAULTS_TO_NONE=0`
restore the old behavior. They are deprecated and will be removed
in 0.17.

Keyword Arguments:

- **as_list** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a lazy stack returns the
entries as a list, one item per stacked tensordict.
Exclusive with `as_padded_tensor` and `as_nested_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **as_padded_tensor** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a lazy stack pads
the entries to the largest shape and returns them as one
tensor: each dim is padded to its largest size, also across
the levels of a lazy stack of lazy stacks. `padding_value`
sets the padding value and `padding_side` sets the side of
every padded dim.
Exclusive with `as_list` and `as_nested_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **as_nested_tensor** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a lazy stack returns
the entries as a nested tensor ([`torch.nested`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/nested.html#module-torch.nested)). `layout`
sets its layout. A lazy stack of lazy stacks raises a
`ValueError`, as a nested tensor has a single nested level.
Exclusive with `as_list` and `as_padded_tensor`.
Defaults to `False`.
- **layout** ([*layout*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.layout)*,**optional*) - the layout of the nested tensor
when `as_nested_tensor=True`: `torch.jagged` or
`torch.strided`. Defaults to `torch.jagged`.
- **padding_side** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - The side of padding. Must be "left" or "right". Defaults to "right".
- **padding_value** (*scalar**or*[*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - The padding value. Defaults to 0.0.

A lazy stack reads the entry of every stacked tensordict and stacks
the results into a new tensor. If the entry shapes differ, the plain
call raises a `RuntimeError`: pass `as_list`, `as_padded_tensor`
or `as_nested_tensor` to get a list, a padded tensor or a nested
tensor instead.

Note

A dense tensordict ignores the keyword arguments today and
warns for `as_list=True` and `as_nested_tensor=True`. Starting
with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to returning a list
or a nested tensor, as a lazy stack does.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": 1, "nested": {"y": 2}}, batch_size=[])
>>> td.get("x")
tensor(1)
>>> td.get(("nested", "y"))
tensor(2)
>>> print(td.get("z"))
None
>>> td.get("z", 0)
0
```

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import lazy_stack
>>> td = lazy_stack([
... TensorDict({"x": torch.ones(1,)}),
... TensorDict({"x": torch.ones(2,) * 2}),
... ])
>>> nested = td.get("x", as_nested_tensor=True)
>>> nested.is_nested, nested.offsets()
(True, tensor([0, 1, 3]))
>>> td.get("x", as_padded_tensor=True)
tensor([[1., 0.],
 [2., 2.]])
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.get_non_tensor

TensorDictBase.get_non_tensor(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, *default=NO_DEFAULT*)

Gets a non-tensor value, if it exists, or default if the non-tensor value is not found.

This method is robust to tensor/TensorDict values, meaning that if the
value gathered is a regular tensor it will be returned too (although
this method comes with some overhead and should not be used out of its
natural scope).

See [`set_non_tensor()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor) for more information
on how to set non-tensor values in a tensordict.

Parameters:

- **key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the location of the NonTensorData object.
- **default** (*Any**,**optional*) - the value to be returned if the key cannot
be found.

Returns: the content of the [`tensordict.tensorclass.NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData),

or the entry corresponding to the `key` if it isn't a
[`tensordict.tensorclass.NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) (or `default` if the
entry cannot be found).

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> data = TensorDict({}, batch_size=[])
>>> data = data.set_non_tensor(("nested", "the string"), "a string!")
>>> assert data.get_non_tensor(("nested", "the string")) == "a string!"
>>> # regular `get` works but returns a NonTensorData object
>>> data.get(("nested", "the string"))
NonTensorData(data=a string!, batch_size=torch.Size([]), device=None)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.init_remote

TensorDictBase.init_remote(*dst: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *group: 'ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *use_broadcast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *_tensorclass_type: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Initializes a remote tensordict by sending its metadata and content.

Two transport modes are available:

- **Point-to-point** (default): uses `send_object_list` +
`dist.send` to transfer metadata and storage to a single
destination rank. Only the sender and receiver need to call the
pair `init_remote` / `from_remote_init`.
- **Broadcast** (`use_broadcast=True`): delegates to
[`broadcast()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast). Metadata and storage are broadcast to
*every* rank in the group. All ranks must participate (receivers
call `from_remote_init(src=..., use_broadcast=True)`). `dst`
is ignored in this mode.

Parameters:

- **dst** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - The rank of the destination process. Required
when `use_broadcast=False` (the default). Ignored when
`use_broadcast=True`.
- **group** (*"ProcessGroup"**,**optional*) - The process group to use for communication. Defaults to None.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device to use for tensor operations. Defaults to None.
- **use_broadcast** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - If `True`, use [`broadcast()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.broadcast) instead
of point-to-point send. Defaults to `False`.

See also

The receiving process should call ~.from_remote_init or an equivalent method to receive and initialize a new tensordict based on the sent metadata.

Examples

```
>>> import os
>>> import torch
>>> import torch.distributed as dist
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, MemoryMappedTensor
>>> import multiprocessing as mp
>>>
>>> def server(queue):
... # Set environment variables for distributed communication
... os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"] = "localhost"
... os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = "29505"
...
... # Initialize the distributed backend
... dist.init_process_group("gloo", rank=0, world_size=2)
...
... # Create a sample tensordict
... td = (
... TensorDict(
... {
... ("a", "b"): torch.ones(2),
... "c": torch.ones(2),
... ("d", "e", "f"): MemoryMappedTensor.from_tensor(torch.ones(2, 2)),
... },
... [2],
... )
... .expand(1, 2)
... .contiguous()
... )
...
... # Send the tensordict metadata and content to the client
... td.init_remote(dst=1)
...
>>> def client(queue):
... # Set environment variables for distributed communication
... os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"] = "localhost"
... os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = "29505"
...
... # Initialize the distributed backend
... dist.init_process_group("gloo", rank=1, world_size=2)
...
... # Receive the tensordict metadata and content from the server
... received_td = TensorDict.from_remote_init(src=0)
...
... # Verify that the received tensordict matches the expected structure and values
... assert set(received_td.keys()) == {"a", "c", "d"}
... assert (received_td == 1).all()
...
... # Signal that the test has completed successfully
... queue.put("yuppie")
>>>
>>> if __name__ == "__main__":
... queue = mp.Queue(1)
...
... # Create and start the server and client processes
... main_worker = mp.Process(target=server, args=(queue,))
... secondary_worker = mp.Process(target=client, args=(queue,))
...
... main_worker.start()
... secondary_worker.start()
...
... try:
... out = queue.get(timeout=10) # Wait for the signal with a timeout
... print(out) # Should print "yuppie"
... finally:
... queue.close()
... main_worker.join(timeout=10)
... secondary_worker.join(timeout=10)
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.irecv

TensorDictBase.irecv(*src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *group_src: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *return_premature: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *init_tag: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *pseudo_rand: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *consolidated: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[torch.Future]] | [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[torch.Future] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Receives the content of a tensordict and updates content with it asynchronously.

Check the example in the [`isend()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.isend.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.isend) method for context.

Parameters:

**src** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the global rank of the source worker. Mutually
exclusive with `group_src`; exactly one of the two must be
provided.

Keyword Arguments:

- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - if set, the specified process group
will be used for communication. Otherwise, the default process group
will be used.
Defaults to `None`.
- **group_src** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the rank of the source worker *relative
to* `group`. Requires `group` to be passed and is mutually
exclusive with `src`. When set, the p2p calls are issued
directly on the group's backend, so `group` may be a
standalone `ProcessGroup` built
against a store (never registered through
[`init_process_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.init_process_group) or
[`new_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.new_group)).
Defaults to `None`.
- **return_premature** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if `True`, returns a list of futures to wait
upon until the tensordict is updated. Defaults to `False`,
i.e. waits until update is completed withing the call.
- **init_tag** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)) - the `init_tag` used by the source worker.
- **pseudo_rand** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if True, the sequence of tags will be pseudo-
random, allowing to send multiple data from different nodes
without overlap. Notice that the generation of these pseudo-random
numbers is expensive (1e-5 sec/number), meaning that it could
slow down the runtime of your algorithm.
This value must match the one passed to [`isend()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.isend.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.isend).
Defaults to `False`.
- **consolidated** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if True, receives a single consolidated storage
tensor directly into `self._consolidated["storage"]`, as
[`recv()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.recv.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.recv) does. The tensordict must already be consolidated
(e.g. from a prior [`from_remote_init()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_remote_init.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_remote_init) call), and all
leaf tensor views update in-place. With
`return_premature=True`, the returned list holds the single
future. `init_tag` and `pseudo_rand` are ignored.
Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

if `return_premature=True`, a list of futures to wait

upon until the tensordict is updated.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.is_consolidated

TensorDictBase.is_consolidated()

Checks if a TensorDict has a consolidated storage.

Returns `False` once [`memmap_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_) moves the leaves out of the
consolidated storage, once an in-place write changes a non-tensor
entry, or once a write replaces, adds or deletes an entry of an
unpickled copy, which is not locked, as the consolidated storage and
metadata no longer match the content. [`consolidate()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate) then
builds a new consolidated copy.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.is_empty

TensorDictBase.is_empty() → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Returns `True` if the tensordict has no leaf.

Empty sub-tensordicts do not count as leaves. A lazy stack counts only
the tensors that all its members share: it returns `True` when they
share none, and warns when some member holds a leaf. Starting with
TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to returning `True` only if
every member is empty.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> TensorDict().is_empty()
True
>>> TensorDict({"nested": TensorDict()}).is_empty()
True
>>> TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(())}).is_empty()
False
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.is_locked

*property*TensorDictBase.is_locked*: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

`True` if the tensordict is locked.

A locked tensordict raises `RuntimeError` on any operation that adds,
removes or renames an entry, or that replaces a leaf with a new tensor.
Writes into the existing leaves still work. See [`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_).

Setting `td.is_locked = True` calls [`lock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.lock_), and
`td.is_locked = False` calls [`unlock_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.unlock_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.unlock_).

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": 0})
>>> td.is_locked
False
>>> td.is_locked = True
>>> td.is_locked
True
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.is_memmap

TensorDictBase.is_memmap() → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Checks if tensordict is memory-mapped.

If a TensorDict instance is memory-mapped, it is locked (entries cannot
be renamed, removed or added). If a `TensorDict` is created with
tensors that are all memory-mapped, this does __not__ mean that `is_memmap`
will return `True` (as a new tensor may or may not be memory-mapped).
Only if one calls tensordict.memmap_() will the tensordict be
considered as memory-mapped.

This is always `True` for tensordicts on a CUDA device.

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

# TensorDictBase.is_non_tensor

TensorDictBase.is_non_tensor(*key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Checks if the value associated with a key is a non-tensor ([`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData)).

Unlike the standalone [`is_non_tensor()`](tensordict.is_non_tensor.html#tensordict.is_non_tensor) function which checks
a value directly, this method checks the **internal representation** of the
stored value, making it reliable for both [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) and
[`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) instances.

This is useful because [`TensorClass`](tensordict.TensorClass.html#tensordict.TensorClass) `get()` unwraps
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) to plain values, so calling
`is_non_tensor(tc.get(key))` on the result would return `False`.
This method always checks the wrapped storage.

Parameters:

**key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the key to check.

Returns:

`True` if the value stored at `key` is a
[`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) or [`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack),
`False` otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> import torch
>>> td = TensorDict({"obs": torch.randn(4)}, [])
>>> td = td.set_non_tensor("label", "cat")
>>> td.is_non_tensor("label")
True
>>> td.is_non_tensor("obs")
False
```

See also

[`set_non_tensor()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.set_non_tensor),
[`get_non_tensor()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get_non_tensor.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get_non_tensor).

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).

---

# TensorDictBase.is_shared

TensorDictBase.is_shared() → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Checks if tensordict is in shared memory.

If a TensorDict instance is in shared memory, it is locked (entries cannot
be renamed, removed or added). If a `TensorDict` is created with
tensors that are all in shared memory, this does __not__ mean that `is_shared`
will return `True` (as a new tensor may or may not be in shared memory).
Only if one calls tensordict.share_memory_() or places the tensordict
on a device where the content is shared by default (eg, `"cuda"`)

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the

# TensorDictBase.isend

TensorDictBase.isend(*dst: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *group: 'torch.distributed.ProcessGroup' | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *group_dst: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *init_tag: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *pseudo_rand: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *consolidated: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*) → [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | List['Work'] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Sends the content of the tensordict asynchronously.

Parameters:

**dst** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the global rank of the destination worker
where the content should be sent. Mutually exclusive with
`group_dst`; exactly one of the two must be provided.

Keyword Arguments:

- **group** (*torch.distributed.ProcessGroup**,**optional*) - if set, the specified process group
will be used for communication. Otherwise, the default process group
will be used.
Defaults to `None`.
- **group_dst** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the rank of the destination worker
*relative to* `group`. Requires `group` to be passed and is
mutually exclusive with `dst`. When set, the p2p calls are
issued directly on the group's backend, so `group` may be a
standalone `ProcessGroup` built
against a store (never registered through
[`init_process_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.init_process_group) or
[`new_group()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.new_group)).
Defaults to `None`.
- **init_tag** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)) - the initial tag to be used to mark the tensors.
Note that this will be incremented by as much as the number of
tensors contained in the TensorDict.
- **pseudo_rand** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if True, the sequence of tags will be pseudo-
random, allowing to send multiple data from different nodes
without overlap. Notice that the generation of these pseudo-random
numbers is expensive (1e-5 sec/number), meaning that it could
slow down the runtime of your algorithm.
Defaults to `False`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if True, a list of futures
will be returned instead of the tag of the last tensor sent.
Defaults to `False`.
- **consolidated** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)) - if True, sends the consolidated storage as a
single tensor (1 message), as [`send()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.send.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.send) does. The tensordict
is consolidated first if needed, which copies every leaf on
each call: a sender that keeps a consolidated copy and
refreshes it with [`update_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.update_) avoids that copy. The
receiver must use `irecv(consolidated=True)` or
`recv(consolidated=True)` and must already hold a
consolidated tensordict with matching schema. With
`return_early=True`, the returned list holds the single
future; otherwise `None` is returned once the message is
sent. `init_tag` and `pseudo_rand` are ignored.
Defaults to `False`.

Example

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from torch import multiprocessing as mp
>>> def client():
... torch.distributed.init_process_group(
... "gloo",
... rank=1,
... world_size=2,
... init_method=f"tcp://localhost:10003",
... )
...
... td = TensorDict(
... {
... ("a", "b"): torch.randn(2),
... "c": torch.randn(2, 3),
... "_": torch.ones(2, 1, 5),
... },
... [2],
... )
... td.isend(0)
...
>>>
>>> def server(queue, return_premature=True):
... torch.distributed.init_process_group(
... "gloo",
... rank=0,
... world_size=2,
... init_method=f"tcp://localhost:10003",
... )
... td = TensorDict(
... {
... ("a", "b"): torch.zeros(2),
... "c": torch.zeros(2, 3),
... "_": torch.zeros(2, 1, 5),
... },
... [2],
... )
... out = td.irecv(1, return_premature=return_premature)
... if return_premature:
... for fut in out:
... fut.wait()
... assert (td != 0).all()
... queue.put("yuppie")
...
>>>
>>> if __name__ == "__main__":
... queue = mp.Queue(1)
... main_worker = mp.Process(
... target=server,
... args=(queue, )
... )
... secondary_worker = mp.Process(target=client)
...
... main_worker.start()
... secondary_worker.start()
... out = queue.get(timeout=10)
... assert out == "yuppie"
... main_worker.join()
... secondary_worker.join()
```

Every tensordict class and every tensorclass has this method. For the
other methods, see [Methods by task](../td.html#api-tensordict-methods).
