# assert_allclose_td

tensordict.assert_allclose_td(*actual: T*, *expected: T*, *rtol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *atol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *equal_nan: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *intersection: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *msg: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = ''*, *prefix: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) = ()*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Asserts that two tensordicts, actual and expected, are element-wise equal within a tolerance for all entries.

This function checks if the elements of the actual tensor are close to the corresponding elements
of the expected tensordict, within a relative tolerance (rtol) and an absolute tolerance (atol).

It is similar to the [`assert_close()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing.html#torch.testing.assert_close) function in PyTorch, but with tensordicts inputs.

Parameters:

- **actual** (*T*) - The tensordict containing actual values.
- **expected** (*T*) - The tensordict containing expected values.
- **rtol** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*|**None**,**optional*) - The relative tolerance parameter. Default is None.
- **atol** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*|**None**,**optional*) - The absolute tolerance parameter. Default is None.
- **equal_nan** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - If True, `NaNs` will be considered equal to `NaNs`. Default is `True`.
- **intersection** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - If True, only the intersection of the two tensordicts will be compared.
Default is `False`.
- **msg** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - An optional message to include in the assertion error if the check fails.
- **prefix** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - a prefix to add to the key for error messages.

Returns:

True if the tensors are close within the specified tolerances, raise an exception otherwise.

Return type:

[*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Raises:

[**AssertionError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#AssertionError) - If the tensordicts are not close within the specified tolerances.

---

# assert_close

tensordict.assert_close(*actual: T*, *expected: T*, *rtol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *atol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *equal_nan: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *intersection: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *msg: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = ''*, *prefix: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) = ()*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

- **expected** (*T*) - The tensordict containing expected values.
- **rtol** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*|**None**,**optional*) - The relative tolerance parameter. Default is None.
- **atol** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*|**None**,**optional*) - The absolute tolerance parameter. Default is None.
- **equal_nan** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - If True, `NaNs` will be considered equal to `NaNs`. Default is `True`.
- **intersection** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - If True, only the intersection of the two tensordicts will be compared.

# cat

tensordict.cat(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*) → T

Concatenates tensordicts along an existing batch dimension `dim`.

Same as `torch.cat(input, dim)`. Every input must have the same keys,
and the same batch size and entry shapes except along `dim`. If the
keys differ, this function raises a `KeyError`. If the shapes do not
match, it raises a `RuntimeError`. To join tensordicts along a new
dimension, use [`stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) or
[`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) (see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to concatenate.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the batch dimension to concatenate along.
Defaults to `0`. A `dim` below `-batch_dims` warns, and is
used on the dims of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict 0.17,
the default will change to raising an `IndexError`, as for a
tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

**out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). Tensorclass inputs give an
instance of their class. If every input is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), the result is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = tensordict.cat(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]),
... TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4), batch_size=[4])]
... )
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([7])
```

---

# collate

tensordict.collate(*batch: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Collates a list of samples into a batch, for [`DataLoader`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.DataLoader).

Pass it as `collate_fn` when the samples are tensordicts or
tensorclasses, or tuples or dicts that hold them, such as
`(td, label)` pairs. The default `collate_fn` of a `DataLoader`
cannot read a tensordict (see [Load data and share it between processes](../../data_loading.html#data-loading)).

The samples are collated by the type of the first one:

- tensordicts and tensorclasses go through
[`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack): the batch
is a dense stack if the samples have the same keys and entry shapes,
and a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) otherwise. A
tensorclass keeps its type.
- tensors go through [`torch.stack()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.stack.html#torch.stack).
- mappings give a `dict` and tuples a tuple (a namedtuple keeps its
type), with each entry collated across the samples.
- anything else goes through [`torch.utils.data.default_collate()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.default_collate).

Parameters:

**batch** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)) - the samples of one batch. Anything other than a
non-empty list is returned as is, for example the tensordict
that a batch sampler reads in one index operation.

Returns:

the collated batch.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, collate
>>> samples = [(TensorDict(x=torch.randn(3)), i) for i in range(10)]
>>> td, label = next(iter(DataLoader(samples, batch_size=4, collate_fn=collate)))
>>> td.batch_size, label
(torch.Size([4]), tensor([0, 1, 2, 3]))
>>> clouds = [TensorDict(points=torch.randn(n, 3)) for n in (5, 2, 7, 3)]
>>> batch = next(iter(DataLoader(clouds, batch_size=4, collate_fn=collate)))
>>> type(batch).__name__, batch.batch_size
('LazyStackedTensorDict', torch.Size([4]))
```

---

# default_is_leaf

tensordict.default_is_leaf(*cls: [Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Returns `True` if a type is not a tensor collection (tensordict or tensorclass), or is a pass-through type.

Pass-through types (like UnbatchedTensor) have `_pass_through=True` and are considered leaves
because their shape doesn't conform to batch dimensions.

Note: NonTensorData types are NOT considered leaves here (they have `_is_non_tensor=True`
but not `_pass_through=True`), so they are excluded from leaves when `leaves_only=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, default_is_leaf
>>> import torch
>>> td = TensorDict(a={}, b="a string!", c=torch.randn(()))
>>> print(td.keys(leaves_only=True, is_leaf=default_is_leaf))
_TensorDictKeysView(['c'],
 include_nested=False,
 leaves_only=True)
```

See also

[`is_leaf_nontensor()`](tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor.html#tensordict.is_leaf_nontensor).

---

# dense_stack_tds

tensordict.dense_stack_tds(*td_list: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)] | [LazyStackedTensorDict](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict)*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → T

Stacks a list of tensordicts, or the tensordicts of a lazy stack, densely if possible.

Use it to turn a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) into a dense
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) when its tensordicts have the same keys
and entry shapes. It is useful when the tensordicts are lazy stacks
themselves, or hold lazy stacks among their nested entries: then
`lazy_stack(td_list).to_tensordict()` is not possible. This function
calls [`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack). So if the tensordicts have
different keys or entry shapes at the top level, the result is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict). See [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking).

Parameters:

- **td_list** (*List**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or*[*LazyStackedTensorDict*](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict)) - the
tensordicts to stack. A [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) is
returned unchanged.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension to stack them along. Required if
`td_list` is a list: without it, a `ValueError` is raised.
Ignored if `td_list` is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), whose `stack_dim` is
used.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the class of the stacked
tensordicts) if they can be stacked densely, a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, lazy_stack
>>> from tensordict import assert_allclose_td, dense_stack_tds
>>> td0 = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(3)},[])
>>> td1 = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(4), "b": torch.zeros(2)},[])
>>> td_lazy = lazy_stack([td0, td1], dim=0)
>>> td_container = TensorDict({"lazy": td_lazy}, [])
>>> td_container_clone = td_container.clone()
>>> td_stack = lazy_stack([td_container, td_container_clone], dim=0)
>>> td_stack
LazyStackedTensorDict(
 fields={
 lazy: LazyStackedTensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 2, -1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 exclusive_fields={
 },
 batch_size=torch.Size([2, 2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False,
 stack_dim=0)},
 exclusive_fields={
 },
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False,
 stack_dim=0)
>>> td_stack = dense_stack_tds(td_stack) # Automatically use the LazyStackedTensorDict stack_dim
>>> td_stack
TensorDict(
 fields={
 lazy: LazyStackedTensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 2, -1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 exclusive_fields={
 1 ->
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 2]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2, 2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False,
 stack_dim=1)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # Note that
>>> # (1) td_stack is now a TensorDict
>>> # (2) this has pushed the stack_dim of "lazy" (0 -> 1)
>>> # (3) this has revealed the exclusive keys.
>>> assert assert_allclose_td(td_stack, dense_stack_tds([td_container, td_container_clone], dim=0))
>>> # This shows it is the same to pass a list or a LazyStackedTensorDict
```

---

# from_consolidated

tensordict.from_consolidated(*filename*)

Reconstructs a tensordict from a consolidated file.

A consolidated file is the single file that
[`consolidate()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.consolidate) writes when you pass it a
`filename`. Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_consolidated()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_consolidated.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_consolidated).

The batch sizes and names are as they were when the file was written.
To write later changes into the file, call
`consolidate(filename=filename)` again on the consolidated tensordict.

Parameters:

**filename** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the path of the file.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). Its entries are views into one
storage that is read from the file.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... _ = td.consolidate(filename=f"{tmpdir}/td.bin")
... loaded = tensordict.from_consolidated(f"{tmpdir}/td.bin")
... print(loaded["b", "c"])
tensor([1., 1., 1.])
```

# from_dataclass

tensordict.from_dataclass(*obj: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***, *dest_cls: [Type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Type) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *frozen: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *autocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *nocast: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *shadow: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *tensor_only: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

Converts a dataclass instance or a type into a tensorclass instance or type, respectively.

This function takes a dataclass instance or a dataclass type and converts it into a tensor-compatible class,
optionally applying various configurations such as auto-batching, immutability, and type casting.

Parameters:

**obj** (*Any*) - The dataclass instance or type to be converted. If a type is provided, a new class is returned.

Keyword Arguments:

- **dest_cls** ([*tensorclass*](tensordict.tensorclass.html#tensordict.tensorclass)*,**optional*) - A tensorclass type to be used to map the data. If not provided, a new
class is created. Without effect if `obj` is a type.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, automatically determines and applies batch size to the resulting object. Defaults to `False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - If auto_batch_size is `True`, defines how many dimensions the output tensordict should have. Defaults to `None` (full batch-size at each level).
- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - The batch size of the TensorDict. Defaults to `None`.
- **frozen** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the resulting class or instance will be immutable. Defaults to `False`.
- **autocast** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, enables automatic type casting for the resulting class or instance. Defaults to `False`.
- **nocast** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, disables any type casting for the resulting class or instance. Defaults to `False`.
- **tensor_only** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, it is expected that all items in tensorclass will be
tensor instances (tensor-compatible, since non-tensor data is converted to tensors if possible).
This can bring significant speed-ups at the cost of flexible interactions with non-tensor data.
Defaults to `False`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, the dataclass type passed will be modified in-place. Defaults to `False`.
Without effect if an instance is provided.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - The device on which the TensorDict will be created. Defaults to `None`.
- **shadow** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - Disables the validation of field names against the names of the tensorclass
members (e.g. `batch_size` or `sum`). Use with caution, as this may cause unintended consequences.
Defaults to False.

Returns:

A tensor-compatible class or instance derived from the provided dataclass.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - If the provided input is not a dataclass instance or type.

Examples

```
>>> from dataclasses import dataclass
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import from_dataclass
>>>
>>> @dataclass
... class X:
... a: int
... b: torch.Tensor
...
>>> x = X(0, 0)
>>> x2 = from_dataclass(x)
>>> print(x2)
X_tc(
 a=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 b=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> X2 = from_dataclass(X, autocast=True)
>>> print(X2(a=0, b=0))
X_tc(
 a=NonTensorData(data=0, batch_size=torch.Size([]), device=None),
 b=Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Note

If a dataclass type is provided, a new class is returned with the specified configurations.
If a dataclass instance is provided, a new instance of the tensor-compatible class is returned.
The auto_batch_size, frozen, autocast, and nocast options allow for flexible configuration of the resulting class or instance.

Warning

Whereas [`from_dataclass()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dataclass.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dataclass) will return a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) instance
by default, this method will return a tensorclass instance or type.

---

# from_dict

tensordict.from_dict(*d*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *names: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a dictionary to a TensorDict.

See also

[`TensorDictBase.from_dict()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_dict) for more information.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, from_dict
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3, 4), "b": torch.randn(3)}
>>> print(from_dict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # nested dict: the nested TensorDict can have a different batch-size
>>> # as long as its leading dims match.
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}
>>> print(from_dict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # Without auto_batch_size=True or batch_dims, the batch size is empty.
>>> from_dict(input_dict).batch_size
torch.Size([])
>>> # To work out the batch size of an existing tensordict, use auto_batch_size_
>>> input_td = TensorDict({"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}, [])
>>> input_td.auto_batch_size_().batch_size
torch.Size([3])
```

# from_module

tensordict.from_module(*module*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *filter_empty: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Puts the parameters and buffers of a module in a tensordict.

Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_module()`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict.from_module), except for the default
of `lock`: this function locks the result by default, and the method
does not. The entries are the parameters and buffers of the
module themselves, not copies. Submodules become nested tensordicts.

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - the module to get the parameters from.
- **as_module** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a
`TensorDictParams` instance is returned,
which can be used to store parameters within a
[`torch.nn.Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module). Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict from the
module is used and unflattened into a TensorDict with the tree
structure of the model. Use it when the module has state-dict
hooks. Defaults to `False`.
- **filter_empty** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, submodules without
parameters or buffers (`nn.ReLU`, for example) get no entry.
If `False`, they get an empty tensordict. Defaults to
`True`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict), or a
`TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> from torch import nn
>>> import tensordict
>>> module = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 4), nn.ReLU())
>>> params = tensordict.from_module(module)
>>> params["0", "weight"] is module[0].weight
True
>>> params.is_locked
True
```

---

# from_modules

tensordict.from_modules(**modules*, *as_module: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lock: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *use_state_dict: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *lazy_stack: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *expand_identical: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Stacks the parameters and buffers of several modules in one tensordict.

The result has one batch dimension, with one element per module. Use it to
run an ensemble of modules that have the same structure with
[`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap) and [`to_module()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_module). Same
as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_modules()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_modules.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_modules): see that page for the
difference between a dense and a lazy result, and for a full ensemble
example.

Parameters:

***modules** (*nn.Module*) - the modules to get the parameters from.

Keyword Arguments:

- **as_module** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a
`TensorDictParams` instance is returned.
Defaults to `False`.
- **lock** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the resulting tensordict is
locked. Defaults to `True`.
- **use_state_dict** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the state-dict of each
module is used. Defaults to `False`.
- **lazy_stack** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the parameters are stacked
in a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) that keeps the
original parameters. If `False`, they are stacked into new
parameters. Exclusive with `as_module`. Defaults to `False`.
- **expand_identical** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, a parameter that is
the same object in every module is expanded instead of stacked.
Ignored when `lazy_stack=True`. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with batch size `[len(modules)]`,
a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) if `lazy_stack=True`,
or a `TensorDictParams` if `as_module=True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> import tensordict
>>> modules = [nn.Linear(3, 4) for _ in range(2)]
>>> params = tensordict.from_modules(*modules)
>>> params.batch_size
torch.Size([2])
>>> params["weight"].shape
torch.Size([2, 4, 3])
```

---

# from_pytree

tensordict.from_pytree(*pytree*, ***, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Converts a pytree to a TensorDict instance.

Lists, tuples, named tuples and dicts become nested tensordicts, and
non-tensor entries record their types, so
[`to_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to_pytree) can rebuild the pytree. Same
as [`tensordict.TensorDict.from_pytree()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_pytree): see that page for the
details.

Parameters:

**pytree** - the pytree to convert.

Keyword Arguments:

- **batch_size** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the batch size of the result.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size is the
largest leading shape that all leaves share. Defaults to
`False`.
- **batch_dims** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - used with `auto_batch_size`: the
number of batch dimensions to keep.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> td = tensordict.from_pytree(
... {"a": torch.zeros(3), "b": (torch.ones(3), torch.ones(3, 2))},
... auto_batch_size=True,
... )
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([3])
>>> td["b", "1"].shape
torch.Size([3, 2])
>>> type(td.to_pytree()["b"]).__name__
'tuple'
```

# from_struct_array

tensordict.from_struct_array(*struct_array*, ***, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *batch_dims: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Converts a structured numpy array to a TensorDict.

See also

[`TensorDictBase.from_struct_array()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.from_struct_array) for more information.

Examples

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from tensordict import from_struct_array
>>> x = np.array(
... [("Rex", 9, 81.0), ("Fido", 3, 27.0)],
... dtype=[("name", "U10"), ("age", "i4"), ("weight", "f4")],
... )
>>> td = from_struct_array(x)
>>> x_recon = td.to_struct_array()
>>> assert (x_recon == x).all()
>>> assert x_recon.shape == x.shape
>>> # Try modifying x age field and check effect on td
>>> x["age"] += 1
>>> assert (td["age"] == np.array([10, 4])).all()
```

# fromkeys

tensordict.fromkeys(*keys: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*, *value: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any) = 0*)

Creates a tensordict from a list of keys and a single value.

Same as [`tensordict.TensorDict.fromkeys()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.fromkeys.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.fromkeys), and as [`dict.fromkeys()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict.fromkeys)
for a dict. The batch size of the result is `[]`.

Parameters:

- **keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys of the new tensordict. A tuple of
strings creates a nested entry.
- **value** (*compatible type**,**optional*) - the value of every entry. Defaults
to `0`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import tensordict
>>> td = tensordict.fromkeys(["a", ("b", "c")], 1)
>>> td["b", "c"]
tensor(1)
```

# is_bool

tensordict.is_bool(**args*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether the last argument is a boolean tensor.

The predicate tests its last argument only, so it can be passed as
`fn(value)` and as `fn(key, value)`: see [`is_inexact()`](tensordict.is_inexact.html#tensordict.is_inexact).

Parameters:

***args** - the value to test is the last one. A key may come before it.

Returns:

`True` if the dtype of the value is `torch.bool`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import is_bool
>>> is_bool(torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.bool)), is_bool("mask", torch.zeros(3))
(True, False)
```

# is_inexact

tensordict.is_inexact(**args*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether the last argument is a floating-point or complex tensor.

The predicate tests its last argument only, so it works both as
`fn(value)`, for example inside a function given to
[`apply()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.apply), and as `fn(key, value)`, for
example as the `cast_filter` of [`to()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.to.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.to).

Parameters:

***args** - the value to test is the last one. A key may come before it.

Returns:

`True` if the dtype of the value is a floating-point or complex dtype.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, is_inexact
>>> is_inexact(torch.zeros(3)), is_inexact("a", torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long))
(True, False)
>>> td = TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(3), i=torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long))
>>> td_bf16 = td.bfloat16(cast_filter=is_inexact)
>>> td_bf16["x"].dtype, td_bf16["i"].dtype
(torch.bfloat16, torch.int64)
```

# lazy_stack

tensordict.lazy_stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*, ***kwargs*) → T

Stacks tensordicts in a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).

The result keeps each input as a separate tensordict, so the inputs can
have different keys, entry shapes and batch sizes. Use it for data whose
size changes from one sample to the next. [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) compares this
function with [`stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) and
[`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack). Same as
[`tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack()`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.lazy_stack), which takes the same
arguments.

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack. It must not be empty. The batch sizes must
have the same number of dimensions. If a dimension differs
between inputs, it is `-1` in the stacked batch size.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim`
below `-batch_dims - 1` warns and wraps around once more (and
raises if it is still out of range).
Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will change to raising
an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a lazy stack to write the result
into. Its batch size must be the stacked batch size.
- **stack_dim_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - a name for the stacked dimension.
- **strict_shape** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch sizes of the
inputs must be equal, or a `RuntimeError` is raised. Defaults
to `False`.

Returns:

a [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict). Tensorclass inputs give
an instance of their class that holds a lazy stack.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = tensordict.lazy_stack(
... [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]),
... TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(4), batch_size=[4])]
... )
>>> type(td).__name__
'LazyStackedTensorDict'
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([2, -1])
>>> td[1]["a"].shape
torch.Size([4])
```

# load

tensordict.load(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *out: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *subpath: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Loads a tensordict that [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save) wrote.

Same as [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.load_memmap.html#tensordict.load_memmap), which takes the same arguments.
See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap) for every argument, and
[Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) for the ways to save and load a tensordict.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory, or the `.tdz` archive file,
that holds the saved tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - if given, the data is cast to that
device. With `"meta"`, no file is read.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the cast to `device`
is not followed by a synchronization. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to load the data into.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - must match the value used to save.
Defaults to `True`.
- **subpath** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the nested tensordict to load,
as a nested key (`("module", "0")`) or a `"/"`-separated path
(`"module/0"`). Only that subtree is read.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"r"` maps the files copy-on-write (in-place
writes stay in memory), `"r+"` maps them shared (in-place writes
reach the files). See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
for the default.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that decompress
the leaves of a compressed archive. It has no effect on other
data. Defaults to `0`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries that
were pickled are unpickled. Only load pickles from trusted
sources.

Returns:

the saved tensordict, of the class it had when it was saved. Its
leaves are [`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... _ = tensordict.save(td, tmpdir)
... loaded = tensordict.load(tmpdir)
... print(loaded["b", "c"].shape)
torch.Size([3, 2])
```

---

# load_memmap

tensordict.load_memmap(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *non_blocking: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *out: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *subpath: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *mode: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *allow_pickle: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Loads a memory-mapped tensordict from disk.

Same as [`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load), and as
[`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) for the ways to save and load a
tensordict.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - the directory, or the `.tdz` archive file,
that holds the saved tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - if given, the data is cast to that
device. With `"meta"`, no file is read.
- **non_blocking** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the cast to `device`
is not followed by a synchronization. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to load the data into.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - must match the value used to save.
Defaults to `True`.
- **subpath** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the nested tensordict to load,
as a nested key (`("module", "0")`) or a `"/"`-separated path
(`"module/0"`). Only that subtree is read.
- **mode** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"r"` maps the files copy-on-write (in-place
writes stay in memory), `"r+"` maps them shared (in-place writes
reach the files). See [`tensordict.TensorDict.load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
for the default.
- **num_threads** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that decompress
the leaves of a compressed archive. It has no effect on other
data. Defaults to `0`.
- **allow_pickle** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries that
were pickled are unpickled. Only load pickles from trusted
sources.

Returns:

the saved tensordict, of the class it had when it was saved. Its
leaves are [`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... _ = tensordict.memmap(td, tmpdir)
... loaded = tensordict.load_memmap(tmpdir)
... print(type(loaded["a"]).__name__)
MemoryMappedTensor
```

# make_tensordict

tensordict.make_tensordict(*input_dict: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *batch_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *auto_batch_size: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Returns a TensorDict created from the keyword arguments or an input dictionary.

If `batch_size` is not specified and `auto_batch_size=True`, the maximum batch size possible is used.

This function works on nested dictionaries too, or can be used to determine the
batch-size of a nested tensordict.

Parameters:

- **input_dict** (*dictionary**,**optional*) - a dictionary to use as a data source
(nested keys compatible).
- ****kwargs** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - keyword arguments as data source
(incompatible with nested keys).
- **batch_size** (*iterable**of*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - a batch size for the tensordict.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*or**compatible type**,**optional*) - a device for the TensorDict.
- **auto_batch_size** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the batch size will be computed automatically.
Defaults to `False`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, make_tensordict
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3, 4), "b": torch.randn(3)}
>>> print(make_tensordict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # alternatively
>>> td = make_tensordict(**input_dict)
>>> # nested dict: the nested TensorDict can have a different batch-size
>>> # as long as its leading dims match.
>>> input_dict = {"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}
>>> print(make_tensordict(input_dict, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # we can also use this to work out the batch sie of a tensordict
>>> input_td = TensorDict({"a": torch.randn(3), "b": {"c": torch.randn(3, 4)}}, [])
>>> print(make_tensordict(input_td, auto_batch_size=True))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: TensorDict(
 fields={
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 4]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# maybe_dense_stack

tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*, ***kwargs*) → T

Stacks tensordicts densely if possible, or in a lazy stack otherwise.

Use it when the inputs usually match, but can differ. If every input has
the same keys, entry shapes and batch size, the result is the dense
stack that [`stack()`](tensordict.stack.html#tensordict.stack) returns. Otherwise, the result is the
lazy stack that [`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) returns. [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)
compares these functions. Same as
[`tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.maybe_dense_stack).

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim` outside
`[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` warns, and is used on the dims
of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will
change to raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into.
- **strict** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - used only with `out`. If `True`, `out`
must have the same keys as the inputs. Defaults to `False`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the tensorclass of the inputs)
if the inputs can be stacked densely, a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict) otherwise.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> same = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(3))]
>>> type(tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(same)).__name__
'TensorDict'
>>> different = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3)), TensorDict(a=torch.ones(4))]
>>> type(tensordict.maybe_dense_stack(different)).__name__
'LazyStackedTensorDict'
```

# memmap

tensordict.memmap(*data: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *copy_existing: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *share_non_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *existsok: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *archive: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Writes all tensors onto memory-mapped tensors in a new tensordict.

Same as [`save()`](tensordict.save.html#tensordict.save), and as
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. Use it to share a tensordict between processes without
copies, or to keep data that is larger than RAM on disk. To convert the
tensordict in place, use [`memmap_()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap_).
See [Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving) and [Load data and share it between processes](../../data_loading.html#data-loading).

Parameters:

- **data** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instance*) - the tensordict to write.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the directory to write to, or a file name that
ends with `".tdz"`. If `None`, the tensors are written to
anonymous shared memory.
- **copy_existing** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, an entry that is already
memory-mapped to a file outside `prefix` raises an error. If
`True`, it is copied. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that write the
files. Defaults to `0`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `num_threads > 0`,
a future of the result is returned. Defaults to `False`.
- **share_non_tensor** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries are
shared between the processes of a node. Defaults to `False`.
- **existsok** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, a tensor file that already
exists under `prefix` raises an error. Defaults to `True`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keys that hold path
separators or special characters are encoded in the file names.
Defaults to `True`.
- **archive** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `prefix` is a file and the
tensordict is written as a single zip archive that
[`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load) can memory-map. If `None`, an archive
is written when `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the compression of the archive
entries: `"stored"`, `"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"` or a
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) constant. Only valid for an archive. Defaults to
`None`, which stores them uncompressed. Only uncompressed
entries load without a copy.

Returns:

a new, locked tensordict whose leaves are
[`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> td_memmap = tensordict.memmap(td)
>>> type(td_memmap["a"]).__name__
'MemoryMappedTensor'
>>> td_memmap.is_locked
True
```

# merge_tensordicts

tensordict.merge_tensordicts(**tensordicts: T*, *callback_exist: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → T

Merges tensordicts together.

Parameters:

***tensordicts** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*or**equivalent*) - the list of tensordicts to merge together.

Keyword Arguments:

**callback_exist** ([*callable*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#callable)*or**Dict**[*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,*[*callable*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#callable)*]**,**optional*) - a callable in case an entry exists in each and every tensordict.
If the entry is present in some but not all tensordicts, or if `callback_exist` is not passed,
update is used and the first non-`None` value in the tensordict sequence will be used.
If a dictionary of callables is passed, it will contain the associated callback function for some of the
nested keys in the tensordicts passed to the function.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import merge_tensordicts, TensorDict
>>> td0 = TensorDict({"a": {"b0": 0}, "c": {"d": {"e": 0}}, "common": 0})
>>> td1 = TensorDict({"a": {"b1": 1}, "f": {"g": {"h": 1}}, "common": 1})
>>> td2 = TensorDict({"a": {"b2": 2}, "f": {"g": {"h": 2}}, "common": 2})
>>> td = merge_tensordicts(td0, td1, td2, callback_exist=lambda *v: torch.stack(list(v)))
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: TensorDict(
 fields={
 b0: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 b1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 b2: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False),
 c: TensorDict(
 fields={
 d: TensorDict(
 fields={
 e: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False),
 common: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False),
 f: TensorDict(
 fields={
 g: TensorDict(
 fields={
 h: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.int64, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(td["common"])
tensor([0, 1, 2])
```

# CudaGraphModule

*class*tensordict.nn.CudaGraphModule(*module: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)] | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)], [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]*, *warmup: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 2*, *in_keys: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] = None*, *out_keys: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] = None*, *device: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Records a function, or a TensorDictModule, as a CUDA graph and replays it.

A replay runs all the recorded kernels with one CPU call, which removes the
CPU overhead of launching them one by one. The first `warmup - 1` calls
run the function on a side stream. The next call records the graph, and
later calls copy their inputs into the graph's buffers and replay it. Each
call checks that the inputs match the recorded ones (see the rules below).
See [CUDA graphs](../../compile.html#compile-cudagraphs) for a worked example.

Without CUDA, the constructor warns, and each call runs the function
directly.

Warning

`CudaGraphModule` is a prototype feature and its API restrictions are likely to change in the future.

Warning

This module requires the wrapped function to meet a few requirements. It is the user responsibility
to make sure that all of these are fulfilled.

> - The function cannot have dynamic control flow. For instance, the following code snippet will fail to be
> wrapped in CudaGraphModule:
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ```
> def func(x):
> if x.norm() > 1:
> return x + 1
> else:
> return x - 1
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> Use [`torch.where()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.where.html#torch.where) instead:
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ```
> def func(x):
> return torch.where(x.norm() > 1, x + 1, x - 1)
> ```
> - The function must execute a code that can be exactly re-run using the same buffers. This means that
> dynamic shapes (changing shape in the input or during the code execution) is not supported. In other words,
> the input must have a constant shape. After the capture, a tensor input with a different shape, or a
> tensordict input with a different batch size or an entry of a different shape, raises a `ValueError`, and
> a tensordict input that lacks one of the `in_keys` raises a `KeyError`.
> - The output of the function must be detached. If a call to the optimizers is required, put it in the input
> function. For instance, the following function is a valid operator:
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ```
> def func(x, y):
> optim.zero_grad()
> loss_val = loss_fn(x, y)
> loss_val.backward()
> optim.step()
> return loss_val.detach()
> ```
> - The inputs must not require gradients. If the function uses `nn.Parameter` instances (or other tensors
> that require gradients), do not pass them as arguments of the call. Read them from the enclosing scope, or
> bind them as default values, as in `def func(x, w=w)`:
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ```
> w = nn.Parameter(torch.randn((), device="cuda"))
> optim = torch.optim.Adam([w], lr=1)
> 
> def func(x): # right: w is not an argument of the call
> optim.zero_grad()
> (x * w).backward()
> optim.step()
> 
> def func(x, w): # wrong: w is passed at each call
> ...
> ```
> - Tensor and tensordict arguments can change between calls, if their device and shape stay the same.
> Arguments that are not tensors (a `float`, a `str`) must not change after the capture. If the
> function takes tensors, a changed value raises a `ValueError`. If it takes a tensordict, the replay uses
> the captured value, ignores the new one and emits a `FutureWarning`. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the
> default will change to raising a `ValueError` there too (pytorch/tensordict#2075).
> The keyword arguments of a tensordict module are its `in_keys` (see [`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch))
> and `tensordict_out`.
> - If the module is a [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase) instance and the output id matches the input
> id, then this identity will be preserved during a call to `CudaGraphModule`, and the outputs written into
> the input are clones of the graph's output buffers. In all other cases, the output will be cloned,
> irrespective of whether its elements match or do not match one of the inputs.
> - In-place writes to the input tensors inside the function (e.g. `x.add_(1)`) do not reach the caller's
> inputs once the graph is captured: the graph reads and writes its own copies of the inputs.
> - The inputs are copied into the graph's buffers, and the graph is replayed, on the current stream. As for any
> CUDA operation, inputs written on another stream must be ordered before the call by the caller, e.g. with
> `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(producer_stream)`. Consecutive calls share the graph's buffers:
> issue them from one stream, or order each call after the previous one in the same way.
> - The replay repeats the branch that each [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) took at
> capture: a graph captured under `set_interaction_type("random")` keeps sampling under
> `set_interaction_type("deterministic")`. The first replay under another interaction type emits a
> `UserWarning`. The check covers only the [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) instances
> inside the wrapped [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module): other code that branches on
> `interaction_type()` (for example an exploration module) and wrapped
> functions that are not modules are not checked; if the wrapped module holds no
> [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule), the replay repeats the captured branch without a
> warning. Capture one `CudaGraphModule` per interaction type whenever the output depends on it.

Warning

`CudaGraphModule` is not an [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module) by design, to discourage gathering parameters
of the input module and passing them to an optimizer.

Parameters:

- **module** (*Callable*) - a function that receives tensors (or tensordict) as input and outputs a
PyTreeable collection of tensors. If a tensordict is provided, the module can be run with keyword arguments
too (see example below).
- **warmup** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the call that records the graph. The first `warmup - 1` calls run the function
on a side stream, the next call records the graph, and later calls replay it. A compiled function needs
enough calls to finish compiling before the capture, for example
`CudaGraphModule(torch.compile(module), warmup=3)`. Defaults to `2`.
- **in_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of**NestedKeys*) - 

the input keys, if the module takes a TensorDict as input.
Defaults to `module.in_keys` if this value exists, otherwise `None`.

Note

If `in_keys` is provided but empty, the module is assumed to receive a tensordict as input.
This is sufficient to make `CudaGraphModule` aware that the function should be treated as a
TensorDictModule, but keyword arguments will not be dispatched. See below for some examples.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of**NestedKeys*) - the output keys, if the module takes and outputs TensorDict as output.
Defaults to `module.out_keys` if this value exists, otherwise `None`.
- **device** ([*device*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*,**optional*) - the device of the stream to use.

Examples

The example needs a CUDA device, so its lines are skipped when the
docs are tested.

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CudaGraphModule, TensorDictModule
>>> # Wrap a simple function
>>> def func(x):
... return x + 1
>>> func = CudaGraphModule(func) 
>>> x = torch.rand((), device='cuda') 
>>> out = func(x) 
>>> assert isinstance(out, torch.Tensor) 
>>> assert out == x+1 
>>> # Wrap a tensordict module
>>> func = TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"])
>>> func = CudaGraphModule(func) 
>>> # This can be called either with a TensorDict or regular keyword arguments alike
>>> y = func(x=x) 
>>> td = TensorDict(x=x) 
>>> td = func(td)
```

Note

Tips on debugging CudaGraphModule errors:

- Errors of the sort of operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream are

to be debugged using a non-compiled version of your code first (compiled code will hide the part of the
code that is responsible for the cross-stream dependency). It can happen because you are
doing inter-device operations which make the capturing stream dependent on other streams.
- Errors like Cannot call CUDAGeneratorImpl::current_seed during CUDA graph capture or other errors originating

from the compiler (not the compiled code!) probably point to a capture of the graph while recompiling.
Capture the recompiles with TORCH_LOGS="+recompiles" python myscript.py and try to fix these.
In general, make sure you are using enough warmup steps.
Please file an issue if you're struggling with these.

# EnsembleModule

*class*tensordict.nn.EnsembleModule(*module: [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*, *num_copies: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *expand_input: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Module that wraps a module and repeats it to form an ensemble.

The constructor makes `num_copies` sets of parameters, each one reset
with the `reset_parameters` method of the submodules. It stacks them in
`ensemble.params_td`, a `TensorDictParams` with
batch size `[num_copies]`. A call runs the module once per copy with
[`torch.vmap()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.vmap.html#torch.vmap), so every output gets a leading dimension of size
`num_copies`.

`ensemble.parameters()` returns the stacked copies, which an optimizer
can train. It also returns the parameters of the original `module`,
which the call does not use.

Parameters:

- **module** (*nn.Module*) - The nn.module to duplicate and wrap.
- **num_copies** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - The number of copies of module to make.
- **expand_input** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, every copy receives the
same input. If `False`, the input must already have a leading
dimension of size `num_copies`, and copy `i` receives entry
`i`. Use `False` for an EnsembleModule placed after another
one, for example `EnsembleModule(cnn)` followed by
`EnsembleModule(mlp)`. Defaults to `True`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, EnsembleModule
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 2))
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['a'], out_keys=['b'])
>>> ensemble = EnsembleModule(mod, num_copies=3)
>>> data = TensorDict({'a': torch.randn(10, 4)}, batch_size=[10])
>>> ensemble(data)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 10, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 10, 2]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3, 10]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

To chain EnsembleModules, set `expand_input=False` on the second one and on those after it.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential, EnsembleModule
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> module = TensorDictModule(torch.nn.Linear(2,3), in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> next_module = TensorDictModule(torch.nn.Linear(3,1), in_keys=['dork'], out_keys=['spork'])
>>> e0 = EnsembleModule(module, num_copies=4, expand_input=True)
>>> e1 = EnsembleModule(next_module, num_copies=4, expand_input=False)
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(e0, e1)
>>> data = TensorDict({'bork': torch.randn(5,2)}, batch_size=[5])
>>> seq(data)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 bork: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 5, 2]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 dork: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 5, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 spork: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 5, 1]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 5]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Define the computation performed at every call.

Should be overridden by all subclasses.

Note

Although the recipe for forward pass needs to be defined within
this function, one should call the `Module` instance afterwards
instead of this since the former takes care of running the
registered hooks while the latter silently ignores them.

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Checks if a module is compatible with TensorDictModule API.

Parameters:
