Returns:

`True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys`
attribute.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Resets the `out_keys` attribute to its original value.

Returns: the same module, with its original `out_keys` values.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Resets the parameters of all the copies of the module.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)) - A TensorDict of parameters for self.module. The batch dimension(s) of the tensordict
denote the number of module copies to reset.

Returns:

A TensorDict of pointers to the reset parameters.

select_out_keys(**out_keys*) → [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Selects the keys that will be found in the output tensordict.

This is useful whenever one wants to get rid of intermediate keys in a
complicated graph, or when the presence of these keys may trigger unexpected
behaviours. The module removes only the out-keys that are not selected:
the other entries of the input tensordict stay in place.

The original `out_keys` can still be accessed via `module.out_keys_source`.

Parameters:

***out_keys** (*a sequence**of**strings**or**tuples**of**strings*) - the
out_keys that should be found in the output tensordict.

Returns: the same module, modified in-place with updated `out_keys`.

The simplest usage is with [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule):

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This feature will also work with dispatched arguments:

```
>>> mod(torch.zeros(()), torch.ones(()))
tensor(3.)
```

This change will occur in-place (ie the same module will be returned
with an updated list of out_keys). It can be reverted using the
[`TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys()`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys) method.

```
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, []))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This will work with other classes too, such as Sequential:

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# InteractionType

*class*tensordict.nn.InteractionType(*value*, *names=<not given>*, **values*, *module=None*, *qualname=None*, *type=None*, *start=1*, *boundary=None*)

Bases: [`StrEnum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.StrEnum)

The rule that a probabilistic module uses to get a value from a distribution.

- `RANDOM`: a sample, from `rsample()` if the distribution has it,
else from `sample()`.
- `MODE`, `MEDIAN`, `MEAN`: the attribute of the same name. If the
distribution has no `mean`, `MEAN` averages `n_empirical_estimate`
samples (see [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule)).
- `DETERMINISTIC`: the `deterministic_sample` attribute. If the
distribution does not have one, the mode for distributions with
enumerable support (Categorical, Bernoulli,
[`OneHotCategorical`](tensordict.nn.distributions.OneHotCategorical.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.OneHotCategorical)) and the mean
for the others. For a distribution class that tensordict does not
know, the module chooses the mean or the mode from the support of the
distribution, and warns.

Set the type for a block of code with [`set_interaction_type`](tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type), or
for one module with its `default_interaction_type` argument. Strings
are accepted, in any case: `InteractionType("RANDOM")`.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import InteractionType
>>> InteractionType("RANDOM")
<InteractionType.RANDOM: 'random'>
>>> InteractionType.from_str("Mode") is InteractionType.MODE
True
```

*classmethod*from_str(*type_str: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*) → InteractionType

Returns the interaction type whose name matches a string, in any case.

Parameters:

**type_str** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - the name, for example `"random"` or `"MODE"`.

# ProbabilisticTensorDictModule

*class*tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(*in_keys: NestedKey | List[NestedKey] | Dict[str, NestedKey], out_keys: NestedKey | List[NestedKey] | None = None, *, default_interaction_type: InteractionType = InteractionType.DETERMINISTIC, distribution_class: type = <class 'tensordict.nn.distributions.continuous.Delta'>, distribution_kwargs: dict | None = None, return_log_prob: bool = False, log_prob_keys: List[NestedKey] | None = None, log_prob_key: NestedKey | None = None, cache_dist: bool = False, n_empirical_estimate: int = 1000, num_samples: int | torch.Size | None = None, generator: torch.Generator | int | NestedKey | None = None*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

A module that builds a distribution from entries of a tensordict and writes a value from it.

The module has no parameters. It reads the distribution parameters at
`in_keys`, builds `distribution_class(**params, **distribution_kwargs)`,
and writes one value at each of the `out_keys`. To compute the parameters
with a network, put a [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) before this
module in a [`ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential). To
get the distribution without a value, call `get_dist()`. To get the
log-probability of a value, call `log_prob()`.

The value depends on the interaction type. The module uses
[`interaction_type()`](tensordict.nn.interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.interaction_type) if it is set (see
[`set_interaction_type`](tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type)). Otherwise it uses
`default_interaction_type`. See [`InteractionType`](tensordict.nn.InteractionType.html#tensordict.nn.InteractionType)
for what each type reads from the distribution. By default the
interaction type is process-wide, so a [`set_interaction_type`](tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type)
block in one thread also changes the value that modules running in other
threads use. Pass `thread_local=True` to keep the block to its own
thread.

With `return_log_prob=True` and the `RANDOM` interaction type, the
module draws and scores the value in one call if the distribution class
defines the method: `dist.rsample_and_log_prob(sample_shape)` if
`dist.has_rsample`, `dist.sample_and_log_prob(sample_shape)`
otherwise. The method returns a `(sample, log_prob)` tuple, with
`log_prob` in the layout of `dist.log_prob`. Define it when
`dist.log_prob(sample)` cannot recover the draw exactly, for example
for a tanh-squashed normal that saturates. Otherwise the module calls
`dist.log_prob` on the sample. The [`torch.distributions`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#module-torch.distributions) classes
do not define these methods;
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) defines both,
and calls them on its components when they define them.

The default `distribution_class` is
[`Delta`](tensordict.nn.distributions.Delta.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.Delta), which always returns its
parameter. With it, the module copies its input to `out_keys`.

If every key in `out_keys` is already in the input and
[`skip_existing()`](tensordict.nn.skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.skip_existing) is `True` (see
[`set_skip_existing`](tensordict.nn.set_skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.set_skip_existing)), the module returns the input
unchanged. Otherwise it computes a new value and overwrites the entry.
See [Modules: TensorDictModule and tensordict.nn](../../modules.html#modules-guide) for a guide.

Log-probability keys

With `return_log_prob=True`, the module also writes the log-probability
of the value. The key depends on [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)
(`False` by default, see [`set_composite_lp_aggregate`](tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate))
and on the number of sampled keys:

| Case | `composite_lp_aggregate()` is `False` (default) | `composite_lp_aggregate()` is `True` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One sampled key, `"action"` | `"action_log_prob"` | `"sample_log_prob"` |
| One nested key, `("agent", "action")` | `("agent", "action_log_prob")` | `"sample_log_prob"` |
| Several sampled keys from a [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution), `"cont"` and `("nested", "disc")` | `"cont_log_prob"` and `("nested", "disc_log_prob")` | The same two entries, and `"sample_log_prob"` with their sum |
| Several probabilistic modules in a [`ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential) | One `<key>_log_prob` entry per sampled key | Each module writes `"sample_log_prob"`, so the entry holds the log-probability of the last module only. Call [`ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.log_prob()`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.log_prob) to get the sum. |

The suffix `_log_prob` goes on the last element of a nested key. Pass
`log_prob_key` (one sampled key) or `log_prob_keys` (several sampled
keys) to choose other keys.

`log_prob()` returns a tensor, except for a
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) while
`composite_lp_aggregate()` is `False`: then it returns a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) with the `<key>_log_prob` entries of the
table. With `True`, the tensor is the sum over the sampled keys and their
event dimensions.

Set [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) before you build the
module. If the value changed since then, `log_prob_key`,
`log_prob_keys`, `log_prob()` and a call with
`return_log_prob=True` can raise a `RuntimeError`.

Parameters:

- **in_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*|**List**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]**|**Dict**[*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]*) - key(s) that will be read from the input TensorDict
and used to build the distribution.
If it is a list of NestedKey or a NestedKey, the leaf (last element) of those keys must match the keywords used by
the distribution class of interest, e.g. `"loc"` and `"scale"` for
the `Normal` distribution and similar.
If in_keys is a dictionary, the keys are the keys of the distribution and the values are the keys in the
tensordict that will get match to the corresponding distribution keys.
- **out_keys** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*|**List**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]**|**None*) - key(s) where the sampled values will be written.
If the input already has these keys, the module overwrites them,
unless [`skip_existing()`](tensordict.nn.skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.skip_existing) is `True`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **default_interaction_type** ([*InteractionType*](tensordict.nn.InteractionType.html#tensordict.nn.InteractionType)*,**optional*) - 

keyword-only argument.
Default method to be used to retrieve
the output value. Should be one of InteractionType: DETERMINISTIC, MODE, MEDIAN, MEAN or RANDOM
(in which case the value is sampled randomly from the distribution). Default
is DETERMINISTIC.

Note

When a value is computed, the module first reads
[`interaction_type()`](tensordict.nn.interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.interaction_type). If it
returns `None` (outside of [`set_interaction_type`](tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type)),
the module uses `default_interaction_type`. TorchRL
collectors sample with `InteractionType.RANDOM` by default
(their `exploration_type` argument).

Note

`MODE` and `MEDIAN` read `dist.mode` and `dist.median`,
and raise `NotImplementedError` if the distribution does
not have them. `MEAN` reads `dist.mean`. If the
distribution does not have a mean, the module averages
`n_empirical_estimate` samples.
- **distribution_class** (*Type**or**Callable**[**[**Any**]**,**Distribution**]**,**optional*) - 

keyword-only argument.
A `torch.distributions.Distribution` class to
be used for sampling.
Default is [`Delta`](tensordict.nn.distributions.Delta.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.Delta).

Note

If the distribution class is of type
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution), the `out_keys`
can be inferred directly from the `"distribution_map"` or `"name_map"`
keyword arguments provided through this class' `distribution_kwargs`
keyword argument, making the `out_keys` optional in such cases.
- **distribution_kwargs** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*,**optional*) - 

keyword-only argument.
Keyword-argument pairs to be passed to the distribution.

Note

if your kwargs contain tensors that you would like to transfer to device with the module, or
tensors that should see their dtype modified when calling module.to(dtype), you can wrap the kwargs
in a [`TensorDictParams`](tensordict.TensorDictParams.html#tensordict.TensorDictParams) to do this automatically.
- **return_log_prob** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - keyword-only argument.
If `True`, the log-probability of the
distribution sample will be written in the tensordict, at the key
given in the table above. Default is `False`.
- **log_prob_keys** (*List**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]**,**optional*) - 

keys where to write the log_prob if `return_log_prob=True`.
Defaults to '<sample_key_name>_log_prob', where <sample_key_name> is each of the `out_keys`.
Custom keys replace these defaults, including for a [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution).
With `return_log_prob=True`, a custom key equal to a sample key, inside one, or holding one raises a
`ValueError` when `distribution_class` is a class (and, for a `CompositeDistribution`,
`distribution_kwargs` holds its `distribution_map`).

Note

This is only available when [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is set to `False`.
- **log_prob_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - 

key where to write the log_prob if `return_log_prob=True`.
Defaults to 'sample_log_prob' when [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is set to True
or '<sample_key_name>_log_prob' otherwise. A custom key that would overwrite a sample raises a
`ValueError`, as for `log_prob_keys`.

Note

When there is more than one sampled key, this is only available when [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is set to `True`.
- **cache_dist** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - 

keyword-only argument. Has no effect.
Default is `False`.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Passing `cache_dist=True` warns, and the argument will be
removed in TensorDict 0.17. Do not pass it.
- **n_empirical_estimate** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - keyword-only argument.
Number of samples to compute the empirical
mean when it is not available. Defaults to 1000.
- **num_samples** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*or*[*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - keyword-only argument.
The number of values per call. The output tensordict is expanded
to `num_samples + batch_size`, and each sampled value gets these
leading dimensions. With the `RANDOM` interaction type, each
value is a new draw. With another interaction type, the module
repeats its one deterministic value `num_samples` times.
Defaults to `None`: one value, no extra dimension.
- **generator** ([*Generator*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Generator.html#torch.Generator)*,*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*, or*[*None*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*,**optional*) - 

keyword-only argument.
Controls the random number generator used when sampling from the distribution
(relevant only for `RANDOM` and `MEAN` interaction types).

- `None` (default): the global PyTorch RNG is used (current behaviour).
- [`torch.Generator`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Generator.html#torch.Generator): this generator is used for every sample. Its state
advances in place across calls, so consecutive forward passes draw distinct
samples. The generator must live on the same device as the distribution
parameters.
- [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int): shorthand for `torch.Generator().manual_seed(int)`; a CPU
generator is created at construction time and used statefully thereafter.
- `NestedKey` (`str` or `tuple`): the generator is fetched from the
input tensordict at this key on every call. The value may be a
[`torch.Generator`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Generator.html#torch.Generator) (used in place, state mutates) or an integer scalar
(read as a stream-key, then a fresh `next_seed` is written back to the
same key after sampling, JAX-PRNG-style).

Note

PyTorch's `Distribution` API does not
accept a `generator` argument. Internally, sampling is wrapped in
[`torch.random.fork_rng()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/random.html#torch.random.fork_rng) and the global RNG state is swapped with the
provided generator's state for the duration of the call. This makes the
approach portable across all distributions (including reparameterized
`rsample` and discrete `sample`). Under `torch.compile`,
the argument is ignored, without a warning.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import (
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential,
... TensorDictModule,
... )
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import NormalParamExtractor
>>> from torch.distributions import Normal, Independent
>>> td = TensorDict(
... {"input": torch.randn(3, 4), "hidden": torch.randn(3, 8)}, [3]
... )
>>> net = torch.nn.GRUCell(4, 8)
>>> module = TensorDictModule(
... net, in_keys=["input", "hidden"], out_keys=["params"]
... )
>>> normal_params = TensorDictModule(
... NormalParamExtractor(), in_keys=["params"], out_keys=["loc", "scale"]
... )
>>> def IndepNormal(**kwargs):
... return Independent(Normal(**kwargs), 1)
>>> prob_module = ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(
... in_keys=["loc", "scale"],
... out_keys=["action"],
... distribution_class=IndepNormal,
... return_log_prob=True,
... )
>>> td_module = ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential(
... module, normal_params, prob_module
... )
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(td_module)
>>> with params.to_module(td_module):
... _ = td_module(td)
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 action: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 action_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 hidden: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 input: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 params: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 scale: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> with params.to_module(td_module):
... dist = td_module.get_dist(td)
>>> print(dist)
Independent(Normal(loc: torch.Size([3, 4]), scale: torch.Size([3, 4])), 1)
>>> # we can also apply the module to the TensorDict with vmap
>>> from torch import vmap
>>> params = params.expand(4)
>>> def func(td, params):
... with params.to_module(td_module):
... return td_module(td)
>>> td_vmap = vmap(func, (None, 0))(td, params)
>>> print(td_vmap)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 action: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 action_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 hidden: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 input: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 params: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 scale: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

build_dist_from_params(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Creates a `torch.distributions.Distribution` instance with the parameters provided in the input tensordict.

Parameters:

Returns:

A `torch.distributions.Distribution` instance created from the input tensordict.

Raises:

[**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - If the input tensordict does not match the distribution keywords.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d

... )

log_prob(*tensordict*, ***, *dist: [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Computes the log-probability of the value stored in `tensordict`.

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input tensordict containing the
distribution parameters and the value at `out_keys`.

Keyword Arguments:

**dist** (*torch.distributions.Distribution**,**optional*) - The distribution instance. Defaults to `None`.
If `None`, the distribution will be computed using the get_dist method.

Returns:

A tensor. For a
[`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) while
[`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is `False`, a
TensorDict with one `<key>_log_prob` entry per sampled key (see
the log-probability key table). For a
composite distribution while it is `True`, the sum of these
entries, which are also written into `tensordict`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import ProbabilisticTensorDictModule
>>> module = ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(
... in_keys=["loc", "scale"], out_keys=["action"], distribution_class=d.Normal
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict(loc=torch.zeros(3), scale=torch.ones(3)))
>>> td["action"]
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
>>> module.log_prob(td)
tensor([-0.9189, -0.9189, -0.9189])
```

*property*log_prob_key

The key where the log-probability is written, when there is one such key.

See the log-probability key table.

Raises:

 changed since the module was built, or if it is `False` and
 the module has several sampled keys (use `log_prob_keys`).

*property*log_prob_keys

The list of keys where the log-probabilities are written.

One key per sampled key when [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)
is `False`, and `[log_prob_key]` when it is `True`. See the
log-probability key table.

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)
 changed since the module was built.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Recursively reset the parameters of the module and its children.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*of**parameters**,**optional*) - If set to None, the module will reset using self.parameters().
Otherwise, we will reset the parameters in the tensordict in-place. This is
useful for functional modules where the parameters are not stored in the module itself.

Returns:

A tensordict of the new parameters, only if parameters was not None.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_param = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> (old_param == net[0].weight).any()
tensor(False)
```

This method also supports functional parameter sampling:

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> old_params = params.clone(recurse=True)
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
```

select_out_keys(**out_keys*) → [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Selects the keys that will be found in the output tensordict.

This is useful whenever one wants to get rid of intermediate keys in a
complicated graph, or when the presence of these keys may trigger unexpected
behaviours. The module removes only the out-keys that are not selected:
the other entries of the input tensordict stay in place.

The original `out_keys` can still be accessed via `module.out_keys_source`.

Parameters:

***out_keys** (*a sequence**of**strings**or**tuples**of**strings*) - the
out_keys that should be found in the output tensordict.

Returns: the same module, modified in-place with updated `out_keys`.

The simplest usage is with [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule):

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This feature will also work with dispatched arguments:

```
>>> mod(torch.zeros(()), torch.ones(()))
tensor(3.)
```

This change will occur in-place (ie the same module will be returned
with an updated list of out_keys). It can be reverted using the
[`TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys()`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys) method.

```
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, []))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This will work with other classes too, such as Sequential:

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential

*class*tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential(**modules: [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase) | [ProbabilisticTensorDictModule](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule)*, *partial_tolerant: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *return_composite: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *selected_out_keys: List[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential)

A [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) that contains one or more [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) instances, and can return their distribution.

Usually the last module is probabilistic and the modules before it
compute its parameters. `get_dist()` returns the distribution, and
`log_prob()` returns the log-probability of a sample. A call to the
module runs every module and writes the sampled values (see
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) for the keys of the
log-probabilities).

`return_composite` decides what `get_dist()` returns when there is
more than one probabilistic module:

- `False`: the distribution of the last module. The other probabilistic
modules only write their values. The last module must be
probabilistic, otherwise the constructor raises `TypeError`.
- `True`: one [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution)
that holds the distributions of all probabilistic modules.

The default chooses `True` if there is more than one probabilistic
module or if the last module is not probabilistic, and `False`
otherwise.

Resulting log-probabilities will be conditional probabilities if samples are interdependent:
whenever

> \[Z = F(X, Y)\]

then the log-probability of Z will be

> \[log(p(z | x, y))\]

Parameters:

***modules** (*sequence**or**OrderedDict**of*[*TensorDictModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*or*[*ProbabilisticTensorDictModule*](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule)) - An ordered sequence of
[`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) instances, usually terminating in a [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule),
to be run sequentially.
The modules can be instances of TensorDictModuleBase or any other function that matches this signature.
Note that if a non-TensorDictModuleBase callable is used, its input and output keys will not be tracked,
and thus will not affect the in_keys and out_keys attributes of the TensorDictSequential.

Keyword Arguments:

- **partial_tolerant** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - stored as an attribute, but
`forward()` does not use it: every module runs on the whole
input, as with `partial_tolerant=False`. To skip the modules whose
input keys are missing, or to run them on the members of a lazy
stack that have the keys, put this module in a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) with
`partial_tolerant=True`. Defaults to `False`.
- **return_composite** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - If True and multiple
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) or
`ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential` instances are found,
a [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) instance will be used.
Otherwise, only the last module will be used to build the distribution.
Defaults to `True` whenever there are more than one probabilistic modules or the last module is not probabilistic.
Errors if return_composite is False and the last module is not probabilistic.
- **selected_out_keys** (*iterable**of**NestedKeys**,**optional*) - the list of out-keys to select. If not provided, all
`out_keys` will be written.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if True, the input tensordict is modified in-place. If False, a new empty
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) instance is created. If "empty", input.empty() is used instead (ie, the
output preserves type, device and batch-size). Defaults to None (relies on sub-modules).

Raises:

- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - If the input sequence of modules is empty.
- [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) - If `return_composite=False` and the final module is not an instance of
 [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) or
 `ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`.

Examples

```
>>> # Typical usage: a single distribution is computed last in the sequence
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import (
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule as Prob,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential as Seq,
... TensorDictModule as Mod,
... )
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>>
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["loc"]),
... Prob(in_keys=["loc"], out_keys=["sample"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... )
>>> input = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3))
>>> td = module(input.copy())
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(module.get_dist(input))
Normal(loc: torch.Size([3]), scale: torch.Size([3]))
>>> print(module.log_prob(td))
tensor([-0.9189, -0.9189, -0.9189])
>>> # Intermediate distributions are ignored when return_composite=False
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["loc"]),
... Prob(in_keys=["loc"], out_keys=["sample0"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["sample0"], out_keys=["loc2"]),
... Prob(in_keys={"loc": "loc2"}, out_keys=["sample1"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... return_composite=False,
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3)))
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 loc2: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample0: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(module.get_dist(input))
Normal(loc: torch.Size([3]), scale: torch.Size([3]))
>>> print(module.log_prob(td))
tensor([-0.9189, -0.9189, -0.9189])
>>> # Intermediate distributions produce a CompositeDistribution when return_composite=True
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["loc"]),
... Prob(in_keys=["loc"], out_keys=["sample0"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["sample0"], out_keys=["loc2"]),
... Prob(in_keys={"loc": "loc2"}, out_keys=["sample1"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... return_composite=True,
... )
>>> input = TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3))
>>> td = module(input.copy())
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 loc2: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample0: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(module.get_dist(input))
CompositeDistribution({'sample0': Normal(loc: torch.Size([3]), scale: torch.Size([3])), 'sample1': Normal(loc: torch.Size([3]), scale: torch.Size([3]))})
>>> print(module.log_prob(td))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 sample0_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample1_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> # Even a single intermediate distribution is wrapped in a CompositeDistribution when
>>> # return_composite=True
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["loc"]),
... Prob(in_keys=["loc"], out_keys=["sample0"], distribution_class=torch.distributions.Normal,
... distribution_kwargs={"scale": 1}),
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["sample0"], out_keys=["y"]),
... return_composite=True,
... )
>>> td = module(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(3)))
>>> print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 loc: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 sample0: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> print(module.get_dist(input))

>>> print(module.log_prob(td))

 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

build_dist_from_params(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Constructs a distribution from the input parameters without evaluating other modules in the sequence.

This method searches for the last [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) in the sequence and uses it to build the distribution.

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input tensordict containing the distribution parameters.

Returns:

The constructed distribution object.

Return type:

D.Distribution

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - If no [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) is found in the sequence.

*property*default_interaction_type

Returns the default_interaction_type of the module using an iterative heuristic.

This property iterates over all modules in reverse order, attempting to retrieve the
default_interaction_type attribute from any child module. The first non-None value
encountered is returned. If no such value is found, a default interaction_type() is returned.

*property*det_part

The modules that compute the distribution parameters.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. Use
`get_dist_params()` to compute the distribution parameters.

*property*device*: [device](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensor_attributes.html#torch.device)*

A deprecated approximation of the module device.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17 because modules may
contain parameters and buffers on multiple devices.

*property*dist_params_keys*: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*

Returns all the keys pointing at the distribution params.

*property*dist_sample_keys*: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*

Returns all the keys pointing at the distribution samples.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) = None*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *_requires_sample: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Reads `in_keys` from `tensordict`, calls the wrapped module, and writes `out_keys`.

If you call the module with tensors instead of a tensordict, the
tensors are put in a new tensordict first (see
[`dispatch()`](tensordict.nn.dispatch.html#tensordict.nn.dispatch)).

Parameters:

**tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - the input tensordict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if given, the outputs
are written into it and it is returned, whatever the value of
`inplace`. Defaults to `None`.
- ****kwargs** - passed to the wrapped module.

Returns:

the tensordict that holds the outputs (see `inplace`).

get_dist(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Returns the distribution resulting from passing the input tensordict through the sequence.

If return_composite is `False`, this method will only consider the last probabilistic module in the sequence.
It runs the modules before it with `get_dist_params()`, so the
intermediate entries are written into `tensordict`.

Otherwise, it will return a [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) instance containing the distributions of all probabilistic modules.
It runs the modules on a shallow copy of `tensordict`, so the input
does not get new entries.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input tensordict.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - Used only when
`return_composite` is `False`: the tensordict where the
intermediate entries are written, instead of `tensordict`.
Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

****kwargs** - Additional keyword arguments passed to the underlying modules.

Returns:

The resulting distribution object.

Return type:

D.Distribution

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - If no probabilistic module is found in the sequence.

Note

When return_composite is `True`, the distributions are conditioned on the previous samples in the sequence.
This means that if a module depends on the output of a previous probabilistic module, its distribution will be conditional.

get_dist_params(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution), [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]

Runs every module except the last one, and returns the tensordict with the distribution parameters.

This method runs the deterministic part of the `ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`
module to obtain the distribution parameters. The interaction type is set to the current global
interaction type if available, otherwise it defaults to the interaction type of the last module.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input tensordict.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - The tensordict where
the parameters are written. If `None`, they are written into
`tensordict`, which is returned. Pass
`tensordict.copy()` to keep the input unchanged.
Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

****kwargs** - Additional keyword arguments passed to the deterministic part of the module.

Returns:

the output tensordict containing the distribution parameters.

Return type:

[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Note

The interaction type is temporarily set to the specified value during the execution of this method.

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*property*is_functional*: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether the wrapped module is a legacy functorch functional module.

Deprecated since version 0.15: This property will be removed in TensorDict 0.17. It only checks
for the `FunctionalModule` classes of the legacy
`functorch.make_functional` API and has no replacement.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Checks if a module is compatible with TensorDictModule API.

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

Returns:

`True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys`
attribute.

log_prob(*tensordict*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***, *dist: [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the log-probability of the input tensordict.

If self.return_composite is `True` and the distribution is a [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution),
this method will return the log-probability of the entire composite distribution.
While [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is `False`, each entry is at
the key where a forward call writes it, as listed in `log_prob_keys`.

Otherwise, it will only consider the last probabilistic module in the sequence.
In that case the intermediate entries are written into `tensordict`,
as in `get_dist()`.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input tensordict, with the
sampled values.
- **tensordict_out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - If given, the
distribution is computed on a copy of `tensordict`, so the
input does not get new entries. Defaults to `None`.

Keyword Arguments:

**dist** (*torch.distributions.Distribution**,**optional*) - The distribution object. If `None`, it will be computed using get_dist.
Defaults to `None`.

Returns:

The log-probability of the input tensordict.

Return type:

[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) or [*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

*property*log_prob_key

The key where the log-probability is written, when there is one such key.

See the [log-probability key table](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#log-prob-keys).

Raises:

[**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)
 changed since the module was built, or if it is `False` and
 the module has several sampled keys (use `log_prob_keys`).

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Resets the `out_keys` attribute to its original value.

Returns: the same module, with its original `out_keys` values.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Recursively reset the parameters of the module and its children.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*of**parameters**,**optional*) - If set to None, the module will reset using self.parameters().
Otherwise, we will reset the parameters in the tensordict in-place. This is
useful for functional modules where the parameters are not stored in the module itself.

Returns:

A tensordict of the new parameters, only if parameters was not None.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_param = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> (old_param == net[0].weight).any()
tensor(False)
```

This method also supports functional parameter sampling:

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> old_params = params.clone(recurse=True)
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
```

select_out_keys(**selected_out_keys*) → [TensorDictSequential](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential)

Selects the keys within the `out_keys` that will be found in the output tensordict.

This change occurs in-place and can be reverted using `reset_out_keys()`.

Parameters:

***selected_out_keys** (*a sequence**of**strings**or**tuples**of**strings*) - the
out_keys that should be found in the output tensordict. Each of them
must be part of the module's `out_keys`.

Returns: the same module, modified in-place with updated `out_keys`.

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if a key in `selected_out_keys` is not part of `out_keys`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule as Mod, TensorDictSequential as Seq
>>> seq = Seq(
... Mod(lambda x: x + 1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... Mod(lambda y: y + 1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> seq.out_keys
['z']
>>> td = seq(TensorDict(x=torch.zeros(())))
>>> assert "y" not in td
>>> td["z"]
tensor(2.)
>>> _ = seq.reset_out_keys()
>>> seq.out_keys
['y', 'z']
```

select_subsequence(*in_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *out_keys: [Iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictSequential](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential)

Returns a new TensorDictSequential with only the modules that are necessary to compute the given output keys with the given input keys.

Parameters:

- **in_keys** - input keys of the subsequence we want to select.
All the keys absent from `in_keys` will be considered as
non-relevant, and modules that *just* take these keys as inputs
will be discarded.
The resulting sequential module will follow the pattern "all
the modules which output will be affected by a different value
for any in <in_keys>".
If none is provided, the module's `in_keys` are assumed.
- **out_keys** - output keys of the subsequence we want to select.
Only the modules that are necessary to get the `out_keys`
will be found in the resulting sequence.
The resulting sequential module will follow the pattern "all
the modules that condition the value or <out_keys> entries."
If none is provided, the module's `out_keys` are assumed.

Returns:

A new TensorDictSequential with only the modules that are necessary according to the given input and output keys.
Modules in a named sequence keep their names, including nested sequences.
The new sequence keeps `partial_tolerant` and `inplace`.
Nested sequences keep their own options the same way.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential as Seq, TensorDictModule as Mod
>>> idn = lambda x: x
>>> module = Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["c"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["e"]),
... )
>>> # select all modules whose output depend on "a"
>>> module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["a"])
TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['b'])
 (1): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['b'],
 out_keys=['c'])
 (2): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['c'],
 out_keys=['d'])
 (3): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['e'])
 ),
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['b', 'c', 'd', 'e'])
>>> # select all modules whose output depend on "c"
>>> module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["c"])
TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['c'],
 out_keys=['d'])
 ),
 in_keys=['c'],
 out_keys=['d'])
>>> # select all modules that affect the value of "c"
>>> module.select_subsequence(out_keys=["c"])
TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['b'])
 (1): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['b'],
 out_keys=['c'])
 ),
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['b', 'c'])
>>> # select all modules that affect the value of "e"
>>> module.select_subsequence(out_keys=["e"])
TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['e'])
 ),
 in_keys=['a'],
 out_keys=['e'])
```

This method propagates to nested sequential:

```
>>> module = Seq(
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["a"], out_keys=["b"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["c"]),
... ),
... Seq(
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["b"], out_keys=["d"]),
... Mod(idn, in_keys=["d"], out_keys=["e"]),
... ),
... )
>>> # select submodules whose output will be affected by a change in "b" or "d" AND which output is "e"
>>> module.select_subsequence(in_keys=["b", "d"], out_keys=["e"])
TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictSequential(
 module=ModuleList(
 (0): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['b'],
 out_keys=['d'])
 (1): TensorDictModule(
 module=<function <lambda> at ...>,
 in_keys=['d'],
 out_keys=['e'])
 ),
 in_keys=['b'],
 out_keys=['d', 'e'])
 ),
 in_keys=['b'],
 out_keys=['d', 'e'])
```

# TensorClassModuleBase

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase(**args: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, ***kwargs: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*)

Bases: [`Generic`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Generic)[`InputClass`, `OutputClass`], [`ABC`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/abc.html#abc.ABC), [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

A TensorClassModuleBase is a base class for modules that operate on TensorClass instances.

TensorClassModuleBase subclasses provide a type-safe way to define modules that work with TensorClass
inputs and outputs. The class automatically extracts input and output type information from the
generic type parameters.

The module can be converted to a TensorDictModule using the `as_td_module()`
method, allowing it to be used in TensorDict-based workflows.

Type Parameters:

InputClass: The input type, must be a TensorClass or Tensor.
OutputClass: The output type, must be a TensorClass or Tensor.

Variables:

- **input_type** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*[**InputClass**]*) - The input type class.
- **output_type** ([*type*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)*[**OutputClass**]*) - The output type class.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... a: torch.Tensor
... b: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... result: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class AddModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, x: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(
... result=x.a + x.b,
... batch_size=x.batch_size
... )
...
>>> module = AddModule()
>>> input_tc = InputTC(a=torch.tensor([1.0]), b=torch.tensor([2.0]), batch_size=[1])
>>> output = module(input_tc)
>>> assert output.result == torch.tensor([3.0])
```

as_td_module() → [TensorClassModuleWrapper](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper)

Convert this module to a module that takes and returns a TensorDict.

This method wraps the TensorClassModuleBase in a
[`TensorClassModuleWrapper`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper), a
[`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase) subclass. Its `in_keys`
and `out_keys` are the fields of the input and output classes. It
returns a new TensorDict with only the output fields (see
[`TensorClassModuleWrapper`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper)).

Returns:

A wrapper that converts between TensorDict

and TensorClass representations.

Return type:

[*TensorClassModuleWrapper*](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper)

Raises:

[**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - If either input_type or output_type is not a TensorClass.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... y: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class MyModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, input: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(y=input.x * 2, batch_size=input.batch_size)
...
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> td_module = module.as_td_module()
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.ones(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> result = td_module(td)
>>> assert (result["y"] == 2).all()
```

*abstract*forward(*x: InputClass*) → OutputClass

Forward pass of the module.

Parameters:

**x** (*InputClass*) - Input instance.

Returns:

Output instance.

Return type:

OutputClass

# TensorClassModuleWrapper

*class*tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleWrapper(*module: [TensorClassModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase)[InputTensorClass, OutputTensorClass]*)

Bases: [`TensorDictModuleBase`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Wrapper class for TensorClassModuleBase objects.

The wrapper takes a TensorDict, converts it to the input TensorClass of the
module, calls the module, and converts the output TensorClass back to a
TensorDict. [`TensorClassModuleBase.as_td_module()`](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.as_td_module) returns one.

The wrapper returns a new TensorDict that holds only the output fields. It
does not write into the input. In a
[`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential), the modules after it cannot
read the input keys, and by default the sequence returns only the
outputs.

Parameters:

**module** ([*TensorClassModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorClassModuleBase)) - The TensorClassModuleBase instance to wrap.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.tensorclass import TensorClass
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorClassModuleBase
>>> import torch
>>>
>>> class InputTC(TensorClass):
... x: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class OutputTC(TensorClass):
... y: torch.Tensor
...
>>> class MyModule(TensorClassModuleBase[InputTC, OutputTC]):
... def forward(self, input: InputTC) -> OutputTC:
... return OutputTC(y=input.x + 1, batch_size=input.batch_size)
...
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> td_module = module.as_td_module()
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(3)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> result = td_module(td)
>>> list(result.keys())
['y']
>>> "y" in td
False
```

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) = None*, *args=None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDict](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

Forward pass converting TensorDict to TensorClass and back.

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)) - Input tensordict. Its entries that are not
fields of the input class are ignored.
- ***args** - Additional positional arguments.
- ****kwargs** - Additional keyword arguments.

Returns:

Output tensordict.

Return type:

[*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)

*property*in_keys

The keys that the module reads from the input tensordict.

*static*is_tdmodule_compatible(*module*)

Checks if a module is compatible with TensorDictModule API.

Parameters:

**module** ([*object*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) - the object to check.

Returns:

`True` if `module` has both an `in_keys` and an `out_keys`
attribute.

*property*out_keys

The keys that the module writes to the output tensordict.

After `select_out_keys()`, only the selected keys. The full list
is in `out_keys_source`.

*property*out_keys_source

All the keys that the module writes, before `select_out_keys()`.

reset_out_keys()

Resets the `out_keys` attribute to its original value.

Returns: the same module, with its original `out_keys` values.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

reset_parameters_recursive(*parameters: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

Recursively reset the parameters of the module and its children.

Parameters:

**parameters** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)*of**parameters**,**optional*) - If set to None, the module will reset using self.parameters().
Otherwise, we will reset the parameters in the tensordict in-place. This is
useful for functional modules where the parameters are not stored in the module itself.

Returns:

A tensordict of the new parameters, only if parameters was not None.

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> old_param = net[0].weight.clone()
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> module.reset_parameters_recursive()
>>> (old_param == net[0].weight).any()
tensor(False)
```

This method also supports functional parameter sampling:

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule
>>> from torch import nn
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2,3), nn.ReLU())
>>> module = TensorDictModule(net, in_keys=['bork'], out_keys=['dork'])
>>> params = TensorDict.from_module(module)
>>> old_params = params.clone(recurse=True)
>>> _ = module.reset_parameters_recursive(params)
>>> (old_params == params).any()
False
```

select_out_keys(**out_keys*) → [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)

Selects the keys that will be found in the output tensordict.

This is useful whenever one wants to get rid of intermediate keys in a
complicated graph, or when the presence of these keys may trigger unexpected
behaviours. The module removes only the out-keys that are not selected:
the other entries of the input tensordict stay in place.

The original `out_keys` can still be accessed via `module.out_keys_source`.

Parameters:

***out_keys** (*a sequence**of**strings**or**tuples**of**strings*) - the
out_keys that should be found in the output tensordict.

Returns: the same module, modified in-place with updated `out_keys`.

The simplest usage is with [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule):

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> import torch
>>> mod = TensorDictModule(lambda x, y: (x+2, y+2), in_keys=["a", "b"], out_keys=["c", "d"])
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = mod.select_out_keys("d")
>>> td = TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, [])
>>> mod(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This feature will also work with dispatched arguments:

```
>>> mod(torch.zeros(()), torch.ones(()))
tensor(3.)
```

This change will occur in-place (ie the same module will be returned
with an updated list of out_keys). It can be reverted using the
[`TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys()`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.reset_out_keys) method.

```
>>> _ = mod.reset_out_keys()
>>> mod(TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros(()), "b": torch.ones(())}, []))
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 c: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 d: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

This will work with other classes too, such as Sequential:

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictSequential
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["y"]),
... TensorDictModule(lambda x: x+1, in_keys=["y"], out_keys=["z"]),
... )
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 y: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> _ = seq.select_out_keys("z")
>>> td = TensorDict({"x": torch.zeros(())}, [])
>>> seq(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 x: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 z: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```
