# CompositeDistribution

*class*tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution(*params: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *distribution_map: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*, ***, *name_map: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *extra_kwargs=None*, *log_prob_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *entropy_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`Distribution`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

A composite distribution that groups multiple distributions together using the TensorDict interface.

This class allows for operations such as log_prob_composite, entropy_composite, cdf, icdf, rsample, and sample
to be performed on a collection of distributions, returning a TensorDict. `cdf()` and `icdf()`
write their results into the input TensorDict.

`log_prob()` and `entropy()` return a TensorDict with one entry
per distribution while [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is
`False` (the default), and one summed tensor while it is `True`. See
the [log-probability key table](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#log-prob-keys) of
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) for the keys that
probabilistic modules write.

Parameters:

- **params** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - A nested key-tensor map where the root entries correspond to sample names, and the leaves
are the distribution parameters. Entry names must match those specified in distribution_map.
- **distribution_map** (*Dict**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**Type**[**torch.distributions.Distribution**]**]*) - Specifies the distribution types to be used.
The names of the distributions should match the sample names in the TensorDict.

Keyword Arguments:

- **name_map** (*Dict**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]**,**optional*) - A mapping of where each sample should be written. If not provided,
the key names from distribution_map will be used. Entries are
matched after [`unravel_key()`](tensordict.unravel_key.html#tensordict.unravel_key).
- **extra_kwargs** (*Dict**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**Dict**]**,**optional*) - A dictionary of additional keyword arguments for constructing the distributions.
- **log_prob_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - 

The key where the aggregated log probability will be stored.
Defaults to 'sample_log_prob'.

Note

if [`tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) returns `False`, the log-probabilities will
be written under ("path", "to", "leaf", "<sample_name>_log_prob")
where ("path", "to", "leaf", "<sample_name>") is the `NestedKey` corresponding to
the leaf tensor being sampled. In that case, the `log_prob_key` argument will be ignored.
- **entropy_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - 

The key where the entropy will be stored. Defaults to 'entropy'

Note

if [`tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) returns `False`, the entropies will
be written under ("path", "to", "leaf", "<sample_name>_entropy")
where ("path", "to", "leaf", "<sample_name>") is the `NestedKey` corresponding to
the leaf tensor being sampled. In that case, the `entropy_key` argument will be ignored.

Note

The batch size of the input TensorDict containing the parameters (params) determines the batch shape of
the distribution. For example, the "sample_log_prob" entry resulting from a call to log_prob will have the
shape of the parameters plus any additional batch dimensions.

See also

[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) and [`ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential)
to learn how to use this class as part of a model.

See also

[`set_composite_lp_aggregate`](tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate) to control the aggregation of the log-probabilities.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution, set_composite_lp_aggregate
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "cont": {"loc": torch.randn(3, 4), "scale": torch.rand(3, 4)},
... ("nested", "disc"): {"logits": torch.randn(3, 10)}
... }, [3])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params,
... distribution_map={"cont": d.Normal, ("nested", "disc"): d.Categorical})
>>> sample = dist.sample((4,))
>>> with set_composite_lp_aggregate(False):
... sample = dist.log_prob(sample)
... print(sample)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 cont_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 nested: TensorDict(
 fields={
 disc_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

cdf(*sample: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes the cumulative distribution function (CDF) for each component distribution in the composite distribution.

This method calculates the CDF for each component distribution and updates the input TensorDict with the results.

Parameters:

**sample** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - A TensorDict containing samples for which to compute the CDF.

Returns:

The input TensorDict updated with <sample_name>_cdf entries for each component distribution.

Return type:

[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "a": {"loc": torch.zeros(2), "scale": torch.ones(2)},
... "b": {"loc": torch.ones(2), "scale": torch.ones(2)},
... }, [2])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params, distribution_map={"a": d.Normal, "b": d.Normal})
>>> sample = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2), b=torch.zeros(2), batch_size=[2])
>>> out = dist.cdf(sample)
>>> out is sample
True
>>> sample["a_cdf"], sample["b_cdf"]
(tensor([0.5000, 0.5000]), tensor([0.1587, 0.1587]))
>>> _ = dist.icdf(sample) # reads the "_cdf" entries
>>> sample["a_icdf"]
tensor([0., 0.])
```

entropy(*samples_mc: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 1*, ***, *aggregate_probabilities: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *include_sum: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes and returns the entropy of the composite distribution.

This method calculates the entropy for each component distribution and optionally sums them.

Parameters:

**samples_mc** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - The number of samples to draw if the entropy does not have a closed-form solution.
Defaults to 1.

Keyword Arguments:

- **aggregate_probabilities** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - Deprecated and ignored. A value other than `None`
emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#DeprecationWarning). Use [`set_composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate)
instead.
- **include_sum** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - Whether to include the summed entropy in the output TensorDict.
Defaults to composite_lp_aggregate(), which defaults to False.

Returns:

If [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)
is `True`, a single tensor with the summed entropies. If it is
`False` (the default), a TensorDict with one `<name>_entropy`
entry per distribution (see `entropy_composite()`).

Return type:

[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) or [*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Note

If a distribution does not implement a closed-form solution for entropy, Monte Carlo sampling is used
to estimate it.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution, set_composite_lp_aggregate
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "cont": {"loc": torch.zeros(3, 4), "scale": torch.ones(3, 4)},
... ("nested", "disc"): {"logits": torch.zeros(3, 10)}
... }, [3])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params,
... distribution_map={"cont": d.Normal, ("nested", "disc"): d.Categorical})
>>> sorted(dist.entropy().keys(True, True), key=str)
[('nested', 'disc_entropy'), 'cont_entropy']
>>> with set_composite_lp_aggregate(True):
... dist.entropy()
tensor([7.9783, 7.9783, 7.9783])
```

entropy_composite(*samples_mc=1*, ***, *include_sum: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes the entropy for each component distribution and returns a TensorDict with individual entropies.

This method is used by the entropy method when [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is `False`.

Parameters:

**samples_mc** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) - The number of samples to draw if the entropy does not have a closed-form solution.
Defaults to 1.

Keyword Arguments:

**include_sum** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - Whether to include the summed entropy in the output TensorDict.
Defaults to composite_lp_aggregate(), which defaults to False.

Returns:

A TensorDict containing the individual entropies for each component distribution,
along with an "entropy" entry containing the summed entropies if include_sum is True.

Return type:

[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Note

If a distribution does not implement a closed-form solution for entropy, Monte Carlo sampling is used
to estimate it.

*classmethod*from_distributions(*params*, *distributions: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey), [Distribution](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)]*, ***, *name_map: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *log_prob_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *entropy_key: [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → CompositeDistribution

Create a CompositeDistribution instance from existing distribution objects.

This class method allows for the creation of a CompositeDistribution by directly providing
a dictionary of distribution instances, rather than specifying distribution types and parameters separately.

Parameters:

- **params** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - A TensorDict that defines the batch shape for the composite distribution.
Only its batch size is used.
- **distributions** (*Dict**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**d.Distribution**]*) - A dictionary mapping nested keys to distribution instances.
These distributions will be used directly in the composite distribution.

Keyword Arguments:

- **name_map** (*Dict**[*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*]**,**optional*) - A mapping of where each sample should be written. If not provided,
the keys of `distributions` are used. Entries are matched
after [`unravel_key()`](tensordict.unravel_key.html#tensordict.unravel_key).
- **log_prob_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - The key where the log probability will be stored.
Defaults to 'sample_log_prob'.
- **entropy_key** ([*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - The key where the entropy will be stored. Defaults to 'entropy'.

Returns:

An instance of CompositeDistribution initialized with the provided distributions.

Return type:

*CompositeDistribution*

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - If a key in name_map cannot be found in the provided distributions.

Note

The batch size of the params TensorDict determines the batch shape of the composite distribution.

Example

```
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution, ProbabilisticTensorDictSequential, ProbabilisticTensorDictModule, TensorDictModule
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>>
>>> # Values are not used to build the dists
>>> params = TensorDict({("0", "loc"): None, ("1", "loc"): None, ("0", "scale"): None, ("1", "scale"): None})
>>> d0 = torch.distributions.Normal(0, 1)
>>> d1 = torch.distributions.Normal(torch.zeros(1, 2), torch.ones(1, 2))
>>>
>>> d = CompositeDistribution.from_distributions(params, {"0": d0, "1": d1})
>>> print(d.sample())
TensorDict(
 fields={
 0: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 1: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([1, 2]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

icdf(*sample: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes the inverse cumulative distribution function (inverse CDF) for each component distribution.

This method requires the input TensorDict to have either a <sample_name>_cdf entry or a <sample_name> entry
for each component distribution. It calculates the inverse CDF and updates the TensorDict with the results.

Parameters:

**sample** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - A TensorDict containing either <sample_name>_cdf or <sample_name> entries
for each component distribution.

Returns:

The input TensorDict updated with <sample_name>_icdf entries for each component distribution.

Return type:

[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Raises:

[**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) - If neither <sample_name> nor <sample_name>_cdf can be found in the input TensorDict for a component distribution.

log_prob(*sample: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes the log-probability of a sample.

Parameters:

**sample** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input sample to compute the log probability for.

Returns:

- `False` (default): a new TensorDict with one `<name>_log_prob`
entry per distribution, for example `cont_log_prob` and
`("nested", "disc_log_prob")` (see `log_prob_composite()`).
`sample` is not modified.
- `True`: one tensor, the sum of the log-probabilities over all
distributions and their event dimensions.

In both cases the batch shape is the batch shape of `sample`.

Return type:

The result depends on [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate)

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution, set_composite_lp_aggregate
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "cont": {"loc": torch.zeros(3, 4), "scale": torch.ones(3, 4)},
... ("nested", "disc"): {"logits": torch.zeros(3, 10)}
... }, [3])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params,
... distribution_map={"cont": d.Normal, ("nested", "disc"): d.Categorical})
>>> sample = TensorDict({"cont": torch.zeros(3, 4), ("nested", "disc"): torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long)}, [3])
>>> lp = dist.log_prob(sample)
>>> sorted(lp.keys(True, True), key=str)
[('nested', 'disc_log_prob'), 'cont_log_prob']
>>> with set_composite_lp_aggregate(True):
... dist.log_prob(sample)
tensor([-5.9783, -5.9783, -5.9783])
```

log_prob_composite(*sample: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, ***, *include_sum: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Computes the log-probability of each component in the input sample and return a TensorDict with individual log-probabilities.

Parameters:

**sample** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)) - The input sample to compute the log probabilities for.

Keyword Arguments:

**include_sum** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - Whether to include the summed log-probability in the output TensorDict.
Defaults to `composite_lp_aggregate()` (`False` by default).

Returns:

A TensorDict containing the individual log-probabilities for each component in the input sample,

along with a "sample_log_prob" entry containing the summed log-probability if include_sum is True.
While [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) is
`True`, the entries are written into `sample`, which is
returned. Otherwise the result is a new TensorDict.

Return type:

Returns the mode of the distribution.

rsample(*shape=None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Generates a sample_shape shaped reparameterized sample or sample_shape
shaped batch of reparameterized samples if the distribution parameters
are batched.

rsample_and_log_prob(*shape=None*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]

Draws a reparameterized sample and returns it with the log-probability of the same draw.

Each component is sampled and scored with its own
`rsample_and_log_prob` method if it has one, and with `rsample` then
`log_prob` otherwise. See `sample_and_log_prob()`.

Parameters:

Defaults to `torch.Size([])`.

Returns:

the sample as returned by
`rsample()`, and its log-probability in the layout of
`log_prob()`.

Return type:

A `(sample, log_prob)` tuple

sample(*shape=None*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Generates a sample_shape shaped sample or sample_shape shaped batch of
samples if the distribution parameters are batched.

sample_and_log_prob(*shape=None*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase), [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)]

Draws a sample and returns it with the log-probability of the same draw.

Each component is sampled and scored with its own `sample_and_log_prob`
method if it has one, and with `sample` then `log_prob` otherwise.
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) calls this method
when it samples with `return_log_prob=True`.

Parameters:

**shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - the leading sample dimensions.
Defaults to `torch.Size([])`.

Returns:

the sample as returned by
`sample()`, and its log-probability in the layout of
`log_prob()`.

Return type:

A `(sample, log_prob)` tuple

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "cont": {"loc": torch.zeros(3, 4), "scale": torch.ones(3, 4)},
... ("nested", "disc"): {"logits": torch.zeros(3, 10)}
... }, [3])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params,
... distribution_map={"cont": d.Normal, ("nested", "disc"): d.Categorical})
>>> sample, lp = dist.sample_and_log_prob()
>>> sorted(lp.keys(True, True), key=str)
[('nested', 'disc_log_prob'), 'cont_log_prob']
```

# Delta

*class*tensordict.nn.distributions.Delta(*param: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *atol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 1e-06*, *rtol: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 1e-06*, *batch_shape: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *event_shape: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [Size](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`Distribution`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.distribution.Distribution)

Delta distribution.

A distribution with all its mass on `param`. `sample()`,
`rsample()`, `mean`, `mode` and
`deterministic_sample` return `param`. `log_prob()` returns
`inf` for a value equal to `param` (within `atol` and `rtol`) and
`-inf` otherwise. It is the default `distribution_class` of
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule).

Parameters:

- **param** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - parameter of the delta distribution;
- **atol** (*number**,**optional*) - absolute tolerance to consider that a tensor matches the distribution parameter;
Default is 1e-6
- **rtol** (*number**,**optional*) - relative tolerance to consider that a tensor matches the distribution parameter;
Default is 1e-6
- **batch_shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - batch shape;
- **event_shape** ([*Size*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/size.html#torch.Size)*,**optional*) - shape of the outcome.
If neither `batch_shape` nor `event_shape` is given, the last
dimension of `param` is the event shape and the others are the
batch shape.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import Delta
>>> dist = Delta(torch.zeros(4, 2))
>>> dist.batch_shape, dist.event_shape
(torch.Size([4]), torch.Size([2]))
>>> dist = Delta(torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0]))
>>> dist.sample()
tensor([1., 2.])
>>> dist.log_prob(torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0])), dist.log_prob(torch.tensor([1.0, 3.0]))
(tensor(inf), tensor(-inf))
```

Returns the log of the probability density/mass function evaluated at

# NormalParamExtractor

*class*tensordict.nn.distributions.NormalParamExtractor(*scale_mapping: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'biased_softplus_1.0'*, *scale_lb: [Number](https://docs.python.org/3/library/numbers.html#numbers.Number) = 0.0001*)

Bases: [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

A non-parametric nn.Module that splits its input into loc and scale parameters.

The scale parameters are mapped onto positive values using the specified `scale_mapping`.

Parameters:

- **scale_mapping** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - positive mapping function to be used with the std.
default = `"biased_softplus_1.0"` (i.e. softplus map with bias such that fn(0.0) = 1.0)
choices: `"softplus"`, `"exp"`, `"relu"`, `"biased_softplus_1"` or `"none"` (no mapping).
See [`mappings()`](tensordict.nn.mappings.html#tensordict.nn.mappings) for more details.
- **scale_lb** (*Number**,**optional*) - The minimum value of the scale (the standard deviation). Default is 1e-4.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import NormalParamExtractor
>>> from torch import nn
>>> module = nn.Linear(3, 4)
>>> normal_params = NormalParamExtractor()
>>> tensor = torch.randn(3)
>>> loc, scale = normal_params(module(tensor))
>>> print(loc.shape, scale.shape)
torch.Size([2]) torch.Size([2])
>>> assert (scale > 0).all()
>>> # with modules that return more than one tensor
>>> module = nn.LSTM(3, 4)
>>> tensor = torch.randn(4, 2, 3)
>>> loc, scale, others = normal_params(*module(tensor))
>>> print(loc.shape, scale.shape)
torch.Size([4, 2, 2]) torch.Size([4, 2, 2])
>>> assert (scale > 0).all()
```

forward(**tensors: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor), ...]

Define the computation performed at every call.

Should be overridden by all subclasses.

Note

Although the recipe for forward pass needs to be defined within
this function, one should call the `Module` instance afterwards
instead of this since the former takes care of running the
registered hooks while the latter silently ignores them.

# OneHotCategorical

*class*tensordict.nn.distributions.OneHotCategorical(*logits: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *probs: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*)

Bases: [`Categorical`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributions.html#torch.distributions.categorical.Categorical)

One-hot categorical distribution.

This class behaves exactly as torch.distributions.Categorical except that it reads and produces one-hot encodings
of the discrete tensors. `sample()`, `mode` and
`deterministic_sample` return `torch.long` one-hot tensors, and
`log_prob()` takes one. When several logits tie for the maximum,
`mode` marks the first, as `torch.distributions.OneHotCategorical`
does.

`rsample()` returns a straight-through sample: its values are one-hot,
and its gradient is the gradient of a
`RelaxedOneHotCategorical` sample with
temperature 1.

Parameters:

- **logits** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - the unnormalized log-probabilities,
with the categories along the last dimension. A last dimension of
size 1 is removed first.
- **probs** ([*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*,**optional*) - the probabilities, as for `logits`.
Pass `logits` or `probs`, not both.
- ****kwargs** - passed to `Categorical`, for
example `validate_args`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import OneHotCategorical
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> dist = OneHotCategorical(logits=torch.tensor([0.0, 2.0, 1.0]))
>>> dist.mode
tensor([0, 1, 0])
>>> dist.sample((2,))
tensor([[0, 0, 1],
 [0, 1, 0]])
>>> dist.log_prob(torch.tensor([0, 1, 0]))
tensor(-0.4076)
```

# TruncatedNormal

*class*tensordict.nn.distributions.TruncatedNormal(*loc: [Number](https://docs.python.org/3/library/numbers.html#numbers.Number) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *scale: [Number](https://docs.python.org/3/library/numbers.html#numbers.Number) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *a: [Number](https://docs.python.org/3/library/numbers.html#numbers.Number) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *b: [Number](https://docs.python.org/3/library/numbers.html#numbers.Number) | [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*, *validate_args: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*)

Bases: [`TruncatedStandardNormal`](tensordict.nn.distributions.truncated_normal.TruncatedStandardNormal.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.truncated_normal.TruncatedStandardNormal)

Truncated Normal distribution.

A normal distribution of mean `loc` and standard deviation `scale`,
restricted to the interval `[a, b]`. Its samples are reparameterized
(`rsample`).

Source: [https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/presentations/truncated_normal.pdf](https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/presentations/truncated_normal.pdf)

Parameters:

- **loc** (*Number**or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the mean of the normal distribution
before truncation.
- **scale** (*Number**or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the standard deviation of the normal
distribution before truncation. Values under `1e-6` are set to
`1e-6`.
- **a** (*Number**or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the lower bound of the support, in the
same units as `loc`.
- **b** (*Number**or*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)) - the upper bound of the support, in the
same units as `loc`.
- **validate_args** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - passed to
`Distribution`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn.distributions import TruncatedNormal
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> dist = TruncatedNormal(loc=torch.zeros(3), scale=torch.ones(3), a=-1.0, b=1.0)
>>> dist.sample()
tensor([-0.0064, 0.4764, -0.7754])
>>> dist.mean
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
>>> TruncatedNormal(loc=5.0, scale=1.0, a=4.0, b=6.0).mean
tensor(5.)
```

cdf(*value: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the cumulative density/mass function evaluated at
value.

Parameters:

**value** (*Tensor*) -

icdf(*value: [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)*) → [Tensor](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/tensors.html#torch.Tensor)

Returns the inverse cumulative density/mass function evaluated at
value.

Parameters:

# inv_softplus

# mappings

tensordict.nn.mappings(*key: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*) → [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)

Returns the function named by `key`.

All the functions except `"none"` (the identity) map real numbers to
non-negative numbers. `"relu"` can return 0, the others return
positive numbers.

Parameters:

**key** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) - one of "softplus", "exp", "relu", "expln",
"biased_softplus" or "none" (no mapping).

Note

If the key begins with `"biased_softplus"`, then it needs to take the following form:
`"biased_softplus_{bias}"` where `bias` can be converted to a floating point number.
Alternatively, the `"biased_softplus_{bias}_{min_val}"` syntax can be used.
The function is then [`biased_softplus`](tensordict.nn.biased_softplus.html#tensordict.nn.biased_softplus) with these arguments:
`softplus(x + inv_softplus(bias - min_val)) + min_val`, which returns
`bias` for a zero input and is always greater than `min_val`.

Note

Custom mappings can be added through `tensordict.nn.add_custom_mapping`.

Returns:

a Callable

# rand_one_hot

Draws a one-hot sample along the last dimension of `values`.

# set_composite_lp_aggregate

*class*tensordict.nn.set_composite_lp_aggregate(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***, *thread_local: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Bases: `_DecoratorContextManager`

Controls whether [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution) log-probabilities and entropies will be aggregated in a single tensor.

When [`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) returns `True`, the log-probs / entropies of [`CompositeDistribution`](tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution.html#tensordict.nn.distributions.CompositeDistribution)
will be summed into a single tensor with the shape of the root tensordict.
When it returns `False` (the default), they are returned as a
TensorDict with one `<name>_log_prob` (or `<name>_entropy`) entry per
sampled key. The value also decides the keys where probabilistic modules
write their log-probabilities: see the [log-probability key table](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#log-prob-keys) of
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule), and
[Modules: TensorDictModule and tensordict.nn](../../modules.html#modules-guide).

The value of composite_lp_aggregate can also be controlled through the COMPOSITE_LP_AGGREGATE environment variable.
It works as a context manager and as a decorator, and `set()` and
`unset()` change it outside of a block.

Parameters:

**mode** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - the value that
[`composite_lp_aggregate()`](tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate.html#tensordict.nn.composite_lp_aggregate) returns inside the
block. Defaults to `True`.

Keyword Arguments:

**thread_local** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the mode applies to the
calling thread only, and blocks that other threads enter do not
change it. Inside the block, blocks without this flag that the
same thread enters stay in that thread too. Threads started inside
the block see the process-wide mode. If `False`, the mode applies
to the whole process. Defaults to `False`.

Note

Threads. The mode is process-wide by default, and is meant to
be set once for the whole process, for example with `set()`
before you build the modules: it decides the keys of the
log-probabilities, which the threads that write them and the threads
that read them must agree on. A `with` block in one thread also
changes the value in other threads at that time, unless it passes
`thread_local=True`. A thread started inside a `thread_local`
block reads the process-wide value, not the block's.

Example

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import CompositeDistribution, set_composite_lp_aggregate
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> params = TensorDict({
... "cont": {"loc": torch.randn(3, 4), "scale": torch.rand(3, 4)},
... ("nested", "disc"): {"logits": torch.randn(3, 10)}
... }, [3])
>>> dist = CompositeDistribution(params,
... distribution_map={"cont": d.Normal, ("nested", "disc"): d.Categorical})
>>> sample = dist.sample((4,))
>>> with set_composite_lp_aggregate(False):
... lp = dist.log_prob(sample)
... print(lp)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 cont_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3, 4]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 nested: TensorDict(
 fields={
 disc_log_prob: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([4, 3]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([4, 3]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> with set_composite_lp_aggregate(True):
... lp = dist.log_prob(sample)
... print(lp)
tensor([[-2.0886, -1.2155, -0.0414],
 [-2.8973, -5.5165, 2.4402],
 [-0.2806, -1.2799, 3.1733],
 [-3.0407, -4.3593, 0.5763]])
```

# set_interaction_type

*class*tensordict.nn.set_interaction_type(*type: [InteractionType](tensordict.nn.InteractionType.html#tensordict.nn.InteractionType) | [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = InteractionType.DETERMINISTIC*, ***, *thread_local: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Bases: `_DecoratorContextManager`

Sets the interaction type of all probabilistic modules inside a block of code, or inside a decorated function.

Inside the block, [`interaction_type()`](tensordict.nn.interaction_type.html#tensordict.nn.interaction_type)
returns `type`, and every [`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule) uses it
instead of its `default_interaction_type`. When the block ends, the
previous value comes back.

Parameters:

**type** ([*InteractionType*](tensordict.nn.InteractionType.html#tensordict.nn.InteractionType)*or*[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the interaction type, for
example `InteractionType.RANDOM` or `"random"` (in any case).
`None` makes each module use its `default_interaction_type`.
Defaults to `InteractionType.DETERMINISTIC`.

Keyword Arguments:

**thread_local** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the interaction type
applies to the calling thread only, and blocks that other threads
enter do not change it. Inside the block, blocks without this flag
that the same thread enters stay in that thread too. Threads
started inside the block see the process-wide interaction type.
If `False`, the interaction type applies to the whole process.
Defaults to `False`.

Note

Threads. By default the interaction type is process-wide: a
`with` block in one thread also changes what the modules running in
other threads at that time use. Pass `thread_local=True` to keep a
block to its own thread. A thread started inside such a block reads
the process-wide value, not the block's.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import distributions as d
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import (
... InteractionType,
... ProbabilisticTensorDictModule,
... set_interaction_type,
... )
>>> module = ProbabilisticTensorDictModule(
... in_keys=["loc", "scale"], out_keys=["action"], distribution_class=d.Normal
... )
>>> td = TensorDict(loc=torch.zeros(3), scale=torch.ones(3))
>>> module(td)["action"] # default_interaction_type is DETERMINISTIC: the mean
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
>>> _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
>>> with set_interaction_type("random"):
... module(td)["action"]
tensor([ 1.5410, -0.2934, -2.1788])
```

It also works as a decorator:

```
>>> @set_interaction_type(InteractionType.MODE)
... def act(td):
... return module(td)
>>> act(td)["action"]
tensor([0., 0., 0.])
```

# set_skip_existing

*class*tensordict.nn.set_skip_existing(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *in_key_attr='in_keys'*, *out_key_attr='out_keys'*, ***, *thread_local: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*)

Bases: `_DecoratorContextManager`

A context manager for skipping existing nodes in a TensorDict graph.

When used as a context manager, it will set the skip_existing() value
to the `mode` indicated, leaving the user able to code up methods that
will check the global value and execute the code accordingly.

When used as a method decorator, it will check the tensordict input keys
and skip the method if the current mode applies to all output keys and they
are already present.
This is not expected to be used as a decorator for methods that do not
respect the following signature: `def fun(self, tensordict, *args, **kwargs)`.

Parameters:

- **mode** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,*[*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - If `True`, it indicates that existing entries in the graph
won't be overwritten, unless they are only partially present. [`skip_existing()`](tensordict.nn.skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.skip_existing)
will return `True`.
If `False`, no check will be performed.
If a list of keys, only modules whose output keys are all in the
list can be skipped. The keys follow TensorDict's nested-key
conventions. If any output key is not in the list, the module runs
and recomputes all of its outputs.
If `None`, the value of [`skip_existing()`](tensordict.nn.skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.skip_existing) will not be
changed. This is intended to be used exclusively for decorating
methods and allow their behaviour to depend on the same class
when used as a context manager (see example below).
Defaults to `True`.
- **in_key_attr** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the input key list attribute
in the module's method being decorated. Defaults to `in_keys`.
- **out_key_attr** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the name of the output key list attribute
in the module's method being decorated. Defaults to `out_keys`.

Keyword Arguments:

**thread_local** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the mode applies to the
calling thread only, and blocks that other threads enter do not
change it. Inside the block, blocks without this flag that the
same thread enters stay in that thread too. Threads started inside
the block see the process-wide mode. If `False`, the mode applies
to the whole process. Defaults to `False`.

Note

Threads. By default the mode is process-wide: a `with` block
in one thread also changes what [`skip_existing()`](tensordict.nn.skip_existing.html#tensordict.nn.skip_existing) returns in
other threads at that time. Pass `thread_local=True` to keep a
block to its own thread. A thread started inside such a block reads
the process-wide value, not the block's.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict.nn import set_skip_existing, skip_existing
>>> with set_skip_existing():
... if skip_existing():
... print("True")
... else:
... print("False")
...
True
>>> print("calling from outside:", skip_existing())
calling from outside: False
```

This class can also be used as a decorator:

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import set_skip_existing, skip_existing, TensorDictModuleBase
>>> class MyModule(TensorDictModuleBase):
... in_keys = []
... out_keys = ["out"]
... @set_skip_existing()
... def forward(self, tensordict):
... print("hello")
... tensordict.set("out", torch.zeros(()))
... return tensordict
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> module(TensorDict({"out": torch.zeros(())}, [])) # does not print anything
TensorDict(
 fields={
 out: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
>>> module(TensorDict()) # prints hello
hello
TensorDict(
 fields={
 out: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

Decorating a method with the mode set to `None` is useful whenever one
wants to let the context manager take care of skipping things from the outside:

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import set_skip_existing, skip_existing, TensorDictModuleBase
>>> class MyModule(TensorDictModuleBase):
... in_keys = []
... out_keys = ["out"]
... @set_skip_existing(None)
... def forward(self, tensordict):
... print("hello")
... tensordict.set("out", torch.zeros(()))
... return tensordict
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> _ = module(TensorDict({"out": torch.zeros(())}, [])) # prints "hello"
hello
>>> with set_skip_existing(True):
... _ = module(TensorDict({"out": torch.zeros(())}, [])) # no print
```

Note

To allow for modules to have the same input and output keys and not
mistakenly ignoring subgraphs, `@set_skip_existing(True)` will be
deactivated whenever the output keys are also the input keys:

```
>>> class MyModule(TensorDictModuleBase):
... in_keys = ["out"]
... out_keys = ["out"]
... @set_skip_existing()
... def forward(self, tensordict):
... print("calling the method!")
... return tensordict
...
>>> module = MyModule()
>>> module(TensorDict({"out": torch.zeros(())}, [])) # runs: in_keys and out_keys overlap
calling the method!
TensorDict(
 fields={
 out: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# pack_memmap

tensordict.pack_memmap(*prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, *archive_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*, ***, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compresslevel: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

Packs a memory-mapped tensordict directory into a single-file zip archive.

The archive entries replicate the directory layout, so the operation is
the exact inverse of [`unpack_memmap()`](tensordict.unpack_memmap.html#tensordict.unpack_memmap) (and of a plain `unzip`).
Tensor payloads are stored uncompressed by default and aligned to
64 bytes, which lets [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
memory-map the archive and expose every leaf as a zero-copy view.

Parameters:

- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - path to a directory previously produced by
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap) and similar methods.
- **archive_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - path of the archive to create. Keep it
outside the source directory. It must not refer to a source file.
An existing file is replaced rather than rewritten in place: a
symlink is followed, but other hard links to the old file keep
the old contents. Overwriting requires write access to both the
existing file and its directory.

Keyword Arguments:

- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - one of `"stored"` (default),
`"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"` or a
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) compression constant. Any value other than
`"stored"` trades memory-mapped (zero-copy) loading for a
smaller file: compressed leaves are decompressed in memory when
accessed.
- **compresslevel** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - compression level forwarded to
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile).

Returns:

the path to the archive.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pack_memmap
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.randn(3), b=TensorDict(c=torch.zeros(3, 2)))
>>> td = td.memmap("./saved_td")
>>> path = pack_memmap("./saved_td", "./saved_td.tdz")
>>> path
PosixPath('saved_td.tdz')
>>> td2 = TensorDict.load_memmap("./saved_td.tdz")
>>> assert (td == td2).all()
```

# pad

tensordict.pad(*tensordict: T*, *pad_size: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*, *value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 0.0*, *inplace: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *safe: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*) → T

Pads all tensors in a tensordict along the batch dimensions with a constant value.

Use it to grow the batch dimensions of one tensordict, for example to
bring samples to a common size before you stack them. To pad and stack a
list of tensordicts in one call, use [`pad_sequence()`](tensordict.pad_sequence.html#tensordict.pad_sequence)
(see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).

Parameters:

- **tensordict** ([*TensorDict*](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict)) - The tensordict to pad
- **pad_size** (*Sequence**[*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*]*) - The padding size by which to pad some batch
dimensions of the tensordict, starting from the first dimension and
moving forward. [len(pad_size) / 2] dimensions of the batch size will
be padded. For example to pad only the first dimension, pad has the form
(padding_left, padding_right). To pad two dimensions,
(padding_left, padding_right, padding_top, padding_bottom) and so on.
pad_size must be even and less than or equal to twice the number of batch dimensions.
- **value** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*,**optional*) - The fill value to pad by, default 0.0.
Non-tensor entries ([`NonTensorData`](tensordict.NonTensorData.html#tensordict.NonTensorData) /
[`NonTensorStack`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack)) keep their values at the
valid positions and hold `None` in the pad slots instead of
`value`.
- **inplace** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - 

If `True`, the input tensordict's identity
and key set are preserved, and each leaf's storage is replaced by
its padded counterpart one at a time. This keeps peak memory close
to the size of the tensordict itself rather than 2x (the case when
a fresh tensordict is allocated alongside the original). The leaf
tensors themselves are still freshly allocated (`pad` necessarily
grows shapes), so this is not a same-storage operation. Defaults to
`False`.

On [`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), `inplace=True` pads
each constituent tensordict along the non-stack dimensions in place
and grows the stack along the stack dimension by appending or
prepending zero-filled copies of the edge constituents; the lazy
stack's identity is preserved.

Warning

If `inplace=True` and the operation fails partway through
(for example an out-of-memory error during a leaf's padding),
the tensordict is left in an inconsistent state: some leaves
will have the new shape and others the old, and the
`batch_size` will not have been updated. Restoring the
original state would require keeping every old leaf alive
until the whole pass succeeded, which would defeat the 1x
memory contract. Use `safe=True` (the default) to catch
the realistic user-error class of failures before any
mutation happens.
- **safe** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - If `True`, validate that the operation
would succeed for every leaf before any mutation occurs. This
catches errors such as negative pad widths that exceed a leaf's
dimension size, leaves that are not paddable, etc., raising
before any in-place rebind. Set to `False` to skip the
pre-flight walk for a small speedup when the inputs are known
to be valid. Defaults to `True`.

Returns:

The padded tensordict. When `inplace=True` this is the same object as
the input; otherwise a new tensordict, or a new tensorclass of the
same type for a tensorclass input.

Note

With `inplace=False`, a lazy stack gives a
[`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict). If the stacked tensordicts have no
names, it has no names either, even when the stack dimension has a
name (from `stack_dim_name` or the `names` setter). To keep that
name, name the dimension of the result again with
[`refine_names()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.refine_names).

Examples

```
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pad
>>> import torch
>>> td = TensorDict({'a': torch.ones(3, 4, 1),
... 'b': torch.ones(3, 4, 1, 1)}, batch_size=[3, 4])
>>> dim0_left, dim0_right, dim1_left, dim1_right = [0, 1, 0, 2]
>>> padded_td = pad(td, [dim0_left, dim0_right, dim1_left, dim1_right], value=0.0)
>>> print(padded_td.batch_size)
torch.Size([4, 6])
>>> print(padded_td.get("a").shape)
torch.Size([4, 6, 1])
>>> print(padded_td.get("b").shape)
torch.Size([4, 6, 1, 1])
```

# pad_sequence

tensordict.pad_sequence(*list_of_tensordicts: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[T]*, *pad_dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *padding_value: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) = 0.0*, *out: T | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *return_mask: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey) = False*, *padding_side: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = 'right'*) → T

Pads a list of tensordicts in order for them to be stacked together in a contiguous format.

Use it to batch samples whose entries differ in size along one
dimension, such as sequences of different lengths. Every entry is padded
along `pad_dim` to the largest size among the inputs, then the inputs
are stacked along a new first dimension. The inputs must have the same
keys, and the entry shapes must match in every dimension other than
`pad_dim`. To keep the inputs unpadded, use
[`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack) instead (see [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking)).

Parameters:

- **list_of_tensordicts** (*List**[*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*]*) - the list of instances to pad and stack.
- **pad_dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the dimension of the entries to pad, counted
from the first dimension of each entry (batch dimensions
included). If it is a batch dimension, the batch size of the
result is padded too. Defaults to `0`.
- **padding_value** (*number**,**optional*) - the padding value. Defaults to `0.0`.
Non-tensor entries are not filled with `padding_value`: when the padded
dim is a batch dimension of the output, they keep their values at the
valid positions and hold `None` in the pad slots, as with
[`pad()`](tensordict.pad.html#tensordict.pad).
- **out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - if provided, the destination where the data will be
written.
- **return_mask** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*or*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)*,**optional*) - if `True`, the result has
a `"masks"` entry. If `return_mask` is a nested key (a string
or a tuple of strings), the masks are stored under that key. The
masks entry is a tensordict with the structure of the stacked
tensordict. Each of its entries is the mask of the valid values,
of size `torch.Size([stack_len, *new_shape])`, where
`new_shape[pad_dim]` is the largest size and the rest of
`new_shape` matches the shape of the input entries. Not
available for tensorclass inputs. Use
[`unpad_sequence()`](tensordict.unpad_sequence.html#tensordict.unpad_sequence) to turn the result back into
the variable-length samples.
- **padding_side** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - `"right"` puts the padding after the
data along `pad_dim`, `"left"` puts it before, as
`get(key, as_padded_tensor=True, padding_side=...)` does on a
lazy stack. The masks mark the data positions on either side.
Defaults to `"right"`.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) (or the tensorclass of the inputs)
with batch size `[len(list_of_tensordicts), *batch_size]`.

Raises:

- [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) - if `list_of_tensordicts` is empty, or if the entry
 shapes differ in a dimension other than `pad_dim`.
- [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) - if `padding_side` is neither `"left"` nor `"right"`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, pad_sequence
>>> list_td = [
... TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros((3, 8)), "b": torch.zeros((6, 8))}, batch_size=[]),
... TensorDict({"a": torch.zeros((5, 8)), "b": torch.zeros((6, 8))}, batch_size=[]),
... ]
>>> padded_td = pad_sequence(list_td, return_mask=True)
>>> print(padded_td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 5, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 6, 8]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.float32, is_shared=False),
 masks: TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 5]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.bool, is_shared=False),
 b: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([2, 6]), device=cpu, dtype=torch.bool, is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)},
 batch_size=torch.Size([2]),
 device=None,
 is_shared=False)
```

# TDGraphModule

*class*tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule(*graph_module: [GraphModule](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule)*, *out_keys: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[NestedKey](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)]*)

Bases: [`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module)

The module that `symbolic_trace()` returns: an FX graph that reads and writes a tensordict.

A call reads the `in_keys` of the traced module from the input
tensordict, runs the graph, and writes the outputs at `out_keys`, into
`tensordict_out` if given, else into the input. The `graph` and
`code` attributes are those of the underlying
[`torch.fx.GraphModule`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule).

This class is a prototype: its API can change without a deprecation
period.

Parameters:

- **graph_module** ([*GraphModule*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.GraphModule)) - the traced graph.
- **out_keys** ([*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*of*[*NestedKey*](tensordict.NestedKey.html#tensordict.NestedKey)) - the keys where the outputs are written.

forward(*tensordict: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*, *tensordict_out: [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, ***kwargs*) → [TensorDictBase](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)

Define the computation performed at every call.

Should be overridden by all subclasses.

Note

Although the recipe for forward pass needs to be defined within
this function, one should call the `Module` instance afterwards
instead of this since the former takes care of running the
registered hooks while the latter silently ignores them.

# symbolic_trace

tensordict.prototype.symbolic_trace(*td_module: [TensorDictModuleBase](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)*) → [TDGraphModule](tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule.html#tensordict.prototype.fx.TDGraphModule)

Traces a TensorDictModule or a TensorDictSequential into an FX graph.

This function is a prototype: its API can change without a deprecation
period. See [FX tracing (prototype)](../../fx.html#fx) for a guide.

It supports a [`TensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModule) that wraps an
[`Module`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html#torch.nn.Module) that [`torch.fx.symbolic_trace()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.symbolic_trace) can trace,
and a [`TensorDictSequential`](tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictSequential) of such modules. A
module that wraps a plain function or a lambda raises a `RuntimeError`
("Unsupported type ... passed for root!"). Other module types, such as
[`ProbabilisticTensorDictModule`](tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule.html#tensordict.nn.ProbabilisticTensorDictModule), raise a
`TypeError`.

Parameters:

**td_module** ([*TensorDictModuleBase*](tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase.html#tensordict.nn.TensorDictModuleBase)) - the module to trace.

Returns:

a `TDGraphModule` with the same inputs and outputs as
`td_module`.

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> from tensordict.nn import TensorDictModule, TensorDictSequential
>>> from tensordict.prototype.fx import symbolic_trace
>>> seq = TensorDictSequential(
... TensorDictModule(nn.Linear(3, 4), in_keys=["x"], out_keys=["hidden"]),
... TensorDictModule(nn.ReLU(), in_keys=["hidden"], out_keys=["y"]),
... )
>>> graph_module = symbolic_trace(seq)
>>> td = graph_module(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2]))
>>> sorted(td.keys())
['hidden', 'x', 'y']
>>> expected = seq(TensorDict(x=torch.ones(2, 3), batch_size=[2]))["y"]
>>> torch.equal(td["y"], expected)
True
```

# refresh_archive_checksums

tensordict.refresh_archive_checksums(*archive_path: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)*) → [Path](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

Recomputes the CRC-32 checksums of a memmap archive after in-place writes.

A tensordict loaded with `TensorDict.load_memmap(path, mode="r+")`
writes through to the archive without updating the CRC-32 that the zip
format stores for each entry. [`load_memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.load_memmap)
does not verify checksums of uncompressed memory-mapped leaves, so this
is only needed before handing the modified archive to tools that do
(`unzip`, [`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile), [`unpack_memmap()`](tensordict.unpack_memmap.html#tensordict.unpack_memmap)).

Parameters:

**archive_path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or**Path*) - path to the archive to fix up.

Returns:

the path to the archive.

---

# save

tensordict.save(*data: [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)*, *prefix: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *copy_existing: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, ***, *num_threads: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, *return_early: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *share_non_tensor: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = False*, *robust_key: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = True*, *archive: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*, *compression: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None) = None*) → [TensorCollection](tensordict.TensorCollection.html#tensordict.TensorCollection)

Saves a tensordict to disk, as memory-mapped files.

Same as [`memmap()`](tensordict.memmap.html#tensordict.memmap), and as
[`memmap()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.memmap), which holds the full text of
every argument. The directory mirrors the key structure of the
tensordict: one file per tensor and one metadata file per nested
tensordict. If `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`, a single archive file is
written instead. Load the result with [`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load). See
[Save and load tensordicts](../../saving.html#saving).

Parameters:

- **data** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instance*) - the tensordict to save.
- **prefix** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*,**optional*) - the directory to write to, or a file name that
ends with `".tdz"`. If `None`, the tensors are written to
anonymous shared memory and nothing is saved to disk.
- **copy_existing** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, an entry that is already
memory-mapped to a file outside `prefix` raises an error. If
`True`, it is copied. Defaults to `False`.

Keyword Arguments:

- **num_threads** ([*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the number of threads that write the
files. Defaults to `0`.
- **return_early** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True` and `num_threads > 0`,
a future of the result is returned. Defaults to `False`.
- **share_non_tensor** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, non-tensor entries are
shared between the processes of a node. Defaults to `False`.
- **robust_key** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, keys that hold path
separators or special characters are encoded in the file names.
Defaults to `True`.
- **archive** ([*bool*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.bool)*,**optional*) - if `True`, `prefix` is a file and the
tensordict is written as a single zip archive that
[`load()`](tensordict.load.html#tensordict.load) can memory-map. If `None`, an archive
is written when `prefix` ends with `".tdz"`. Defaults to
`None`.
- **compression** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*int*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.int.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.int)*,**optional*) - the compression of the archive
entries: `"stored"`, `"deflate"`, `"bzip2"`, `"lzma"` or a
[`zipfile`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html#module-zipfile) constant. Only valid for an archive. Defaults to
`None`, which stores them uncompressed. Only uncompressed
entries load without a copy.

Returns:

a new, locked tensordict whose leaves are
[`MemoryMappedTensor`](tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor.html#tensordict.MemoryMappedTensor) instances backed by the
saved files. `data` itself is not changed.

Examples

```
>>> import tempfile
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), b={"c": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=[3])
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
... saved = tensordict.save(td, tmpdir)
... print(saved.is_locked, type(saved["a"]).__name__)
... loaded = tensordict.load(tmpdir)
True MemoryMappedTensor
```

# set_capture_non_tensor_stack

*class*tensordict.set_capture_non_tensor_stack(*mode: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*)

Controls whether identical non-tensor data should be captured when stacked.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Capturing identical non-tensor data (`set_capture_non_tensor_stack(True)`
or `CAPTURE_NONTENSOR_STACK=1`) is deprecated and will be removed in
TensorDict 0.17. Use [`NonTensorStack.data`](tensordict.NonTensorStack.html#tensordict.NonTensorStack.data)
to get the single value of a stack of identical values.
`set_capture_non_tensor_stack(False)`, the default, does not warn,
and will keep working, doing nothing, after the removal.

Sets the default of get to None and silences deprecation warnings during calls to get that result in a KeyError.

Deprecated since version 0.15: Since v0.7, [`get()`](tensordict.TensorDictBase.get.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase.get) returns `None` for a
missing key by default. This function, and setting `TD_GET_DEFAULTS_TO_NONE`
to a false value, are deprecated and will be removed in TensorDict 0.17.
Use `td[key]` to raise a `KeyError` for a missing key.

Parameters:

**set_to_none** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) - whether the default of get should be None, or should get raise a KeyError if
no default is passed and the key is absent from the TensorDict.
Defaults to True.

# set_printoptions

*class*tensordict.set_printoptions(***, *verbose: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) = True*, ***kwargs*)

Controls which attributes appear in TensorDict's `__repr__` output.

Use it as a context manager or a decorator to change the options for a
block of code, or call `set_printoptions(...).set()` to change them
for the rest of the program. [Printing and display](../../printing.html#printing) describes every option
with examples.

Parameters:

- **verbose** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*,**optional*) - if `False`, the device, dtype and
`is_shared` attributes are hidden, unless a keyword argument
sets them. Defaults to `True`.
- ****kwargs** - the options to set: `show_batch_size`, `show_device`,
`show_is_shared`, `show_shape`, `show_field_device`,
`show_dtype`, `show_field_is_shared`, `show_grad`,
`show_is_contiguous`, `show_is_view`, `show_storage_size`,
`plain`, `sort_keys` and `compact`. An unknown option
raises a `TypeError`. `compact=True` prints each entry on
one line as its dtype and its shape after the batch dims
(`f32[3]`); see [Printing and display](../../printing.html#printing).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict, set_printoptions
>>> td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3])
>>> with set_printoptions(verbose=False):
... print(td)
TensorDict(
 fields={
 a: Tensor(shape=torch.Size([3]))},
 batch_size=torch.Size([3]))
```

# stack

tensordict.stack(*input: Sequence['T']*, *dim: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) = 0*, ***, *out=None*) → T

Stacks tensordicts into one dense tensordict along a new dimension `dim`.

Same as `torch.stack(input, dim)`. Every input must have the same keys,
entry shapes and batch size. If they do not, this function raises a
`RuntimeError`. To fall back to a lazy stack when the inputs differ, use
[`maybe_dense_stack()`](tensordict.maybe_dense_stack.html#tensordict.maybe_dense_stack). To always get a lazy stack, use
[`lazy_stack()`](tensordict.lazy_stack.html#tensordict.lazy_stack). [Stacking and variable-size data](../../concepts/stacking.html#stacking) compares these functions.

Parameters:

- **input** (*sequence**of*[*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*or**tensorclass instances*) - the
tensordicts to stack.
- **dim** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*,**optional*) - the new dimension. Defaults to `0`. A `dim` outside
`[-batch_dims - 1, batch_dims]` warns, and is used on the dims
of the leaves. Starting with TensorDict 0.17, the default will
change to raising an `IndexError`, as for a tensor.

Keyword Arguments:

**out** ([*TensorDictBase*](tensordict.TensorDictBase.html#tensordict.TensorDictBase)*,**optional*) - a tensordict to write the result
into. Its batch size must be the stacked batch size.

Returns:

a [`TensorDict`](tensordict.TensorDict.html#tensordict.TensorDict) whose batch size is
`batch_size[:dim] + [len(input)] + batch_size[dim:]`. Tensorclass
inputs give an instance of their class. If every input is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict), the result is a
[`LazyStackedTensorDict`](tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict.html#tensordict.LazyStackedTensorDict).

Examples

```
>>> import torch
>>> import tensordict
>>> from tensordict import TensorDict
>>> tds = [TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(3), batch_size=[3]) for _ in range(2)]
>>> td = tensordict.stack(tds, dim=1)
>>> td.batch_size
torch.Size([3, 2])
>>> type(td).__name__
'TensorDict'
```
